articles.title: Barcelona Completes Transfer Deadline Day Deal For Gabriel Jesus From Arsenal
articles.summary: Gabriel Jesus completed a transfer deadline day move from Arsenal to Barcelona on Tuesday on a three-year contract.
articles.body: Gabriel Jesus completed a transfer deadline day move from Arsenal to Barcelona on Tuesday on a three-year contract. The 29-year-old Brazil striker was part of Arsenal's Premier League title-winning squad last season after lifting four league crowns with Manchester City. He joins Spanish champion Barcelona following the departure of Robert Lewandowski at the end of last season. Jesus joined Arsenal in 2022 after six trophy-laden seasons at City. Despite enduring an injury-disrupted time at the Emirates Stadium, he was part of the squad that ended the London club's 22-year wait to be crowned English champion. Jesus is the latest arrival in a busy transfer window for Barcelona, following deals for Anthony Gordon, Rodri, Joao Cancelo, Karim Adeyemi and Dominik Livakovic. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Philadelphia 76ers legend reacts to heartfelt Naomi Osaka tribute as US Open outfit proved to be love letter to the NBA icon
articles.summary: International Sports News: Naomi Osaka opened her US Open campaign with an outfit built entirely around one man, and it is Allen Iverson. The four-time Grand Slam champion walke.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka opened her US Open campaign with an outfit built entirely around one man, and it is Allen Iverson. The four-time Grand Slam champion walked onto Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing his signature headband and arm sleeve, tucked under a gray hooded robe covered in newspaper clippings from her own career, paired with a wide, floor-length skirt.She won the match in straight sets, but the outfit had people talking before a ball was even struck. By Monday night, Iverson had noticed too, and he had something to say about it.Naomi Osaka's US Open outfit pays tribute to Allen IversonNaomi Osaka beat unseeded Russian Anastasia Zakharova 7-6, 7-6 in her opening match, but the real story arrived before the first serve. Her robe, worn as she entered Ashe, was stitched with burnout newspaper clippings tracing her own career, a nod to Iverson's habit of turning up in whatever he wanted rather than what the league expected. She kept it simple when asked why. "It's my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot," she said afterward.The look was part of a broader Nike push linking tennis to basketball at this year's tournament. Aryna Sabalenka wore a mesh jersey in an orange shade tied to the Knicks for her own first-round win earlier that day.Osaka had already signaled where her loyalty sat days before, wearing a shirt printed with an old SLAM magazine cover of Iverson and calling him someone who reshaped how NBA players dress, on and off the court.Allen Iverson reacts to Naomi Osaka's tributeOsaka admitted she had never actually met Iverson, only that she hoped he would see the outfit. And he did. The Hall of Famer posted his reaction on Instagram within hours: "Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you."Designers Téla D'Amore and Ev Bravado, who built the piece, said Osaka and stylist Law Roach sent them two reference photos of Iverson in his headband, then gave them roughly 30 hours to construct the rest around that image. The result carried Iverson's off-court signature almost exactly: the sweats, the sleeve, the headband worn low.Osaka's run of statement outfits continues this seasonThis is far from Osaka's first fashion statement of the year. At the Australian Open, she arrived under a wide-brimmed veil and parasol in a jellyfish-inspired look. At the French Open, she unveiled a black corset made from her own old Nike gear before switching into a gold dress she compared to the Eiffel Tower at night. At Wimbledon, she worked within the tournament's all-white rule to build a kimono-inspired outfit honoring Japanese design traditions.Osaka finished Monday's win with 11 aces against three double faults, despite 30 unforced errors along the way. She now moves on to face Kateřina Siniaková in the second round on Wednesday.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFC West Predictions: Can The Seahawks Secure A Second Consecutive Title?
articles.summary: Nick Wright, Chris Broussard and Danny Parkins made their NFC West predictions on Tuesday's edition of First Things First.
articles.body: In arguably the hardest division in the NFL, two teams have emerged as not just potential winners of the NFC West, but as potential candidates to lift the Lombardi trophy In February. However, the question remains: Can the Seahawks go back-to-back or will the Rams take back the NFC West? The Rams won the offseason with their defensive additions in defensive end Myles Garrett and safety Trent McDuffie. But the biggest win came from the return of four-time Pro Bowler Aaron Donald, who came out of retirement to play alongside Garrett in Los Angeles. However, the reigning Super Bowl champions make a strong case to win a second consecutive NFC West title. Returning quarterback Sam Darnold and wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba make a strong case to keep the hardware for a second year in a row. Here's how all three First Things First co-hosts' predictions for the NFC West this season. Nick Wright's NFC West Predictions: 1.Seattle Seahawks 2.Los Angeles Rams 3.San Francisco 49ers 4.Arizona Cardinals Nick Wright elected for a repeat NFC West title for the Seattle Seahawks, followed by the Los Angeles Rams, the San Francisco 49ers and the Arizona Cardinals in last. Even with the loss of Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, Wright says the Seahawks are still in position to be a 14-win team led by quarterback Sam Darnold. "They’re going to go 14-3. Aside from losing Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker, which is a massive loss, I don’t know why they wouldn’t be awesome again," Wright said on Tuesday's edition of First Things First. "They were dominant all of last year…Do we see post-Super Bowl win, a free Sam Darnold where he’s actually better than we’ve ever seen him before? It’s certainly on the board." As the Seahawks rebuild at running back, the Rams are a team whose additions make them one of the most intriguing teams in the NFL. However, Wright said LA is due for an 11-6 record and won't be ‘quite as good as everyone expects them to be.' Wright placed the 49ers in third because of last season's injury overhaul, the overuse of running back Christian McCaffrey and the departure of their former defensive coordinator. "So many injuries. I don’t trust the wide receivers. I think they will miss Robert Saleh. They pressed the CMC button so many times last year," Wright said. Which leaves Arizona in last place, according to Wright. The Cardinals closed out their 2025 campaign with a 3-14 record, and could be set up to repeat the record this season. "They’re going 3-14. They might be the worst team in the league, and they definitely have the toughest schedule in the league," Wright said. Chris Broussard's NFC West Predictions: 1.Los Angeles Rams 2.Seattle Seahawks 3.San Francisco 49ers 4.Arizona Cardinals Chris Broussard went a different direction and chose the Rams as his NFC West favorites. The Rams have had an eventful offseason with the addition of star defensive linemen Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. When it came to putting the Super Bowl champions in second, Broussard made his point about where they could be after the big win. "I still have them making the playoffs. I just think they're not going to be quite as good as last year. I think it’s kind of natural. Macdonald is great. They just won a Super Bowl," Broussard said. When talking about the 49ers, who came in third on Broussard's list, the amount of injuries and the departure of former defensive coordinator Robert Saleh is a big reason Broussard did not make them a playoff team. "Half the team is hurt. And I don’t have them in the postseason. I would be pleasantly surprised if Brock (Purdy) went out there and cooked…I agree with Nick, they’re going to miss Saleh. He kept that defense together last year," Broussard said. While Broussard placed the Arizona Cardinals last, he tabbed rookie Jeremiyah Love as someone to watch on Arizona's roster this fall. "We all know who’s finishing last, the Arizona Cardinals. I do want to see what Jeremiyah Love does," Broussard said. Danny Parkins' NFC West Predictions: 1.Seattle Seahawks 2.Los Angeles Rams 3.San Francisco 49ers 4.Arizona Cardinals Danny Parkins followed similar suit of Wright's picks, placing the Seahawks first. Parkins' reasoning for Seattle's first place prediction comes from being overlooked because they won a Super Bowl. "I think everyone is continuing to overlook a Super Bowl team that blew out the 49ers in their playoff game. Blew out the Patriots in the Super Bowl," Parkins said. "I have the Seahawks being the forgotten champion and running it back." The Rams were labeled as Parkins' "super team," which was only reinforced after Los Angeles traded for Myles Garrett, which led to Aaron Donald returning along with a returning Matthew Stafford. As the 49ers also come in third place on Parkins' list, the difference he made is his prediction that San Francisco will make the playoffs. "The San Francisco 49ers, I have them making the playoffs," Parkins said. "They won 12 games, and basically everything went wrong…it’s been a weird offseason, but they also added Mike Evans. They were the third most injured team last year, and they won 12 games." San Francisco was without star defensive linemen Nick Bosa and Fred Warner, tight end George Kittle, and wide receiver Ricky Pearsall. However, the 49ers managed to make their way to an NFC Divisional win over the Philadelphia Eagles. As the Cardinals, once again, fell last place in the predictions, Parkins did not count out offensive stars like Marvin Harrison Jr, Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride. However, it's not enough. "I like a few of the players on the Cardinals. I do think Marvin Harrison is in line for a good year. I think McBride is excellent. Jeremiyah Love is excellent. The problem is, everything else."

articles.title: NFL Catchup: Christian McCaffrey Back At Practice; Bears Unsure On DB Kyler Gordon
articles.summary: Keep up with the latest news from around the NFL as the calendar flips to September and opening night a week away.
articles.body: Teams across the league continue managing injuries and fine-tuning rosters as the regular season inches closer. San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey was back at practice Tuesday, while Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles addressed ongoing uncertainty surrounding cornerback Kyler Gordon's return. New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson remains sidelined while rehabilitating an ankle injury and when Pittsburgh Steelers Joey Porter Jr. was asked about whether or not he will play for the Steelers in Week 1, he responded, "I don't know." Keep up with the latest news from around the league on Tuesday. McCaffrey Looking Explosive At Practice After weeks of speculation, San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is back on the field practicing. He was seen on a Tuesday afternoon making cuts and looking explosive during team drills, showing he's ready for the Week 1 opener. McCaffrey missed more than two weeks of training camp while dealing with what was described as general "tightness." It’s unclear if the issue was related to the Achilles tendinitis that sidelined him in 2024 or simply a precaution for other injuries he’s dealt with over his career. However, this should be an encouraging sign as he looks fully healthy heading into Australia, when the 49ers take on the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1. McCaffrey is coming off the heaviest workload season of his career, accumulating a career-high 413 total touches. He logged 311 rushes for 1,202 yards and 10 touchdowns, while adding 102 receptions for 924 yards and seven touchdowns in the passing game. If McCaffrey stays healthy, the 49ers offense could make serious noise in a competitive NFC West. The additions of Mike Evans and rookie De’Zhaun Stribling, alongside a healthy McCaffrey and Brock Purdy, make this offense one of the most intriguing units in the league. Bears GM Unsure When Kyler Gordon Will Return Chicago Bears general manager Ryan Poles expressed uncertainty Tuesday regarding when defensive back Kyler Gordon will return to action as he continues to recover from a lingering calf injury. Gordon, who signed a three-year, $40 million contract extension in April 2025, has appeared in just five games since signing the deal and has been sidelined throughout the entire offseason. When asked Tuesday if he envisions Gordon playing for Chicago during the upcoming 2026 season, Poles offered a guarded response. "I don't know. I would hope so," Poles said to reporters Tuesday. "I still have hope there. He's going to have to continue to work hard and get back to playing." Poles declined to provide specifics on Gordon's recovery process, confirming that the defensive back is working with team trainers while also consulting outside medical personnel. "When people come back from injuries, there's different things that happen," Poles said. "Sometimes they return fast, sometimes they're slow. So it's really a timing thing and a healing thing and a confidence thing. Anytime you have an injury and you're coming back from something, there's discomfort that you have to push through, and that's what it comes down to. So we haven't been able to get over that hump, and we're not progressing as fast as we would like." As Gordon remains on the reserve list, the Bears made additional roster moves Tuesday. Chicago placed safety Coby Bryant and tight end Hayden Large on injured reserve, leaving open the flexibility to designate both for return later in the season. To fill those roster spots, the Bears signed defensive tackle James Lynch and linebacker Jack Sanborn to the active 53-man roster. Joey Porter Jr. Noncommittal On Week 1 Status Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. returned to practice on Tuesday after dealing with a back injury, but remained noncommittal about whether he will play in the season opener without a new contract. Entering the final year of his rookie contract, Porter addressed his Week 1 availability when asked if he would suit up against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13. "I don't know," Porter said. "I've got to talk to the front office and my agents about that one." General manager Omar Khan stated Monday that the team wants Porter to remain with the franchise long-term, but Pittsburgh holds a long-standing policy of ceasing all contract negotiations once the regular season begins. While Porter acknowledged that navigating the business side has been difficult, he noted that teammates and coaches have offered support as he continues preparing. "I could hope and think all day, but it’s really up to the front office and what they want to do with this team," Porter said. "So all I can do is just show up every day to work and be prepared." Henderson Dealing With Ankle Injury New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson hasn’t practiced in over a week due to an ankle injury suffered in training camp. It’s an injury that has flown under the radar, especially with Ashton Jeanty also grabbing headlines after suffering a scary ankle injury of his own.Henderson returned to Patriots practice on Tuesday afternoon but has not yet been cleared for full participation, ESPN first reported. While he continues to rehab a right ankle injury on the side, he was seen walking normally in the locker room, but his Week 1 status is unclear. He is coming off a productive rookie season in the Patriots offense. On just 180 carries, Henderson racked up 911 yards and nine touchdowns, while adding 35 receptions for 221 receiving yards and a score in the pass game.If Henderson can’t suit up next Wednesday night against the Seattle Seahawks, Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to see a full workload. Even though Stevenson is already the featured back, he could turn into a true three-down workhorse early in the season. Injury News & Notes

articles.title: Willie Peters: Hull KR head coach targeting perfect farewell with Super League play-off place on the line
articles.summary: Willie Peters’ Hull KR need one more victory to secure their Super League play-off spot; they can make it into the top six with a win over Huddersfield Giants on Friday September 4; round 26 of Super League begins on Thursday September 3 live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Barring a miracle, this will be Willie Peters' final contest before he heads to take over as head coach of the NRL's new PNG Chiefs, who join the competition in 2028.

Peters made history for the Robins, bringing home their first trophy since 1895, first Grand Final win, and a quadruple that was capped off with a World Club Challenge win over Brisbane Broncos.

Now, he wants to end his time at Sewell Group Craven Park with a victory that would secure Hull KR a place in the top six and see St Helens miss out on the play-offs for the first time in their history.

However, if Hull KR lose to the Giants and St Helens beat Leigh Leopards on the same night, live on Sky Sports , it will all come down to their final round clash on Friday September 11.

For Peters, the magnitude of the game is not lost on him, especially since he employs a mentality that the next game is always the most important one.

"We win this game, we are in the six. If we don't win this game, then naturally we're fighting to survive in the six," he said.

"I always talk about it is our next game, which is always the most important.

"There's two things that give it reason to. Obviously, it's our last home game here, so it's important that we finish the year strong.

"Potentially, we could still make it [if we lose], but when you're relying on opposition teams, it's more than likely it's not going to happen.

"So it's important that we finish our last home game at Craven Park with a strong performance, because we haven't done that the last two times we've been here."

Of course, the priority for Peters on Friday is securing the two points that keep their title defence alive. But it will also be a significant night for the Hull KR boss, as it is set to be the last time he occupies the coaching box at Craven Park - the scene of so much of his success with Hull KR.

Indeed, it will be his chance to soak in, one last time, what east Hull means to him.

"Every time I've coached here, I've been the proudest coach in the world sitting in that box at Craven Park and nothing will change this week," Peters said.

"I've got one more opportunity to do that. I just want to be able to look out on the park one more time and look at this team that this community and fanbase are proud of.

"It's important they do that with their actions this week and we put in a strong performance for the fans.

"When I come down to Craven Park, I always drive down and watch people come in, and that's east Hull for me.

"You see families walk in, partners, best friends - there's all these different walks of people from different lives coming together to do the same thing, and that's supporting their team.

"I'm proud every time I sit in that box to coach this club, and I get the opportunity to do that one more time."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Current LSU football stars embrace NFL players returning to college
articles.summary: LSU football's leadership council gave head coach Lane Kiffin the thumbs up to add former NFL signees.
articles.body:
Several LSU football players defended LSU's attempt to add ex-NFL players to the roster. LSU is hoping to have former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright and former Ole Miss defensive tackle Zxavian Harris on the field this year. Both were undrafted free agents in 2026 and neither made an NFL roster, opening up the door for a college return.

LSU's bold roster moves have drawn attention across the sport and put a spotlight on the program, as many conferences and universities oppose players who have signed pro contracts returning to college. LSU linebacker Whit Weeks is unfazed.

"I don't think it's really a distraction for us in the building at all," Weeks said, "With the last four years, how college football's gone, you kind of just got to be ready to expect anything.

Weeks said LSU head coach Lane Kiffin approached the leadership council last week and asked if the team was open to bringing these players in.

"He said if we don't want them to come back and play, then they won't come back. But we were like, if that's the rule, we might as well go ahead and take these guys. But as far as what I've seen from them in the short amount of time that I've gotten to know them, it's just the experience that they bring and how they go about their business."

LSU tight end Trey'Dez Green had positive words to say and has enjoyed sharing a position room with Wright.

"Even if it means less catches, less yards, I'm all about bringing this national championship back to Baton Rouge. Dae'Quan is amazing. I had a chance to talk with him, and it's just been going up. We clicked ever since we met each other," Green said.

LSU center Braelin Moore was also happy to add Wright, according to Matt Moscona. Moore and Wright played together at Virginia Tech.

Fans have wondered what current LSU players feel about the new additions with the season so close, but it appears the locker room is united behind the idea.

Still, it remains unclear if Wright or Harris will even play a snap for LSU. Legal proceedings are ongoing, but there should be more information by the end of the week.

LSU opens the 2026 season vs. Clemson on Saturday night in Tiger Stadium.

articles.title: Packers bringing back international kicker prospect on practice squad
articles.summary: The Packers are bringing back K Lenny Krieg -- who was with the team to start training camp -- as the international exemption player on the practice squad.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are bringing back kicker Lenny Krieg -- who was with the team to start training camp -- as the international exemption player on the practice squad, per Bill Huber of Packers on SI .

Krieg, a native of Berlin, Germany, spent three days with the Packers to start camp. He was released when the Packers needed to add veteran long snapper Cal Adomitis to the roster with Matt Orzech on the PUP list.

Now, Krieg is back -- providing a backup kicking option on the practice squad and allowing the Packers to carry the maximum 17 players on the practice squad. Each team is allowed an exemption for an international player on the practice squad, allowing for the pro development of players from outside the United States.

Krieg spent the 2025 season on the practice squad of the Atlanta Falcons. He was with the New York Jets between January and June of this year. Per Huber, Krieg has trained with former Falcons Younghoe Koo while waiting for his next opportunity.

Krieg, 24, has never kicked in a regular season game, but he did kick for the Falcons during the preseason last August.

Krieg is replacing tight end Thomas Yassmin -- who was waived injured at final cuts -- as the team's international player. The Packers still have two more slots on the practice squad to fill.

articles.title: ESPN reporter shares what made Tom Brady even more ‘special’ than Kobe Bryant
articles.summary: Tom Brady is widely recognised as the greatest to ever do it in the NFL having shown a mentality unlike no other. The 49-year-old has now transitioned into t...
articles.body:
Tom Brady is widely recognised as the greatest to ever do it in the NFL having shown a mentality unlike no other.

The 49-year-old has now transitioned into the world of broadcasting, having inked a huge deal with Fox Sports.

Brady made a lot of sacrifices during his career to enjoy the success he did with both the New England Patriots and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

One ESPN reporter has recalled his first meeting with Brady during his rookie season, which has stuck with him throughout his own career.

Looking back on the success Brady enjoyed, reporter Seth Wickersham has shared what he found different about Brady and the late Kobe Bryant.

What separated Tom Brady from the late great Kobe Bryant

Brady secured himself seven Super Bowl rings during his career and Bryant won five NBA championships during his time in the league.

Make no mistake about it, these are two of the greatest sportsmen to ever live, but Wickersham feels there is something about Brady that makes him even more special.

"Kobe was motivated, but he was different, obviously, because he had the spotlight on him as a first-round pick from the beginning, so he had something to live up to," the ESPN reporter told Rich Eisen.

"Whereas Brady was under the radar for a bit. I think with Brady, it's just the little things he said over the years that you look back on and think, "Those were the clues."

Brady was selected by the Patriots with the 199 overall pick in the 2000 NFL Draft, whereas Bryant was the 13 overall pick in the 1996 NBA Draft.

"He once said, "Football's always come easy to me." That doesn't mean he never had to work at it, because he obviously worked his tail off, but those are the moments where you realise he had an innate sense of the game and took to it in a special way. In retrospect, you see those little moments as lore or little clues."

Some may argue that this would have only put more pressure on Bryant to perform, given the stock spent to bring him to Charlotte.

However, Brady's sixth-round selection certainly makes for a better success story.

articles.title: Could Luke Evangelista’s trade from Nashville Predators to New Jersey Devils reshape his NHL career
articles.summary: NHL News: Explore how Luke Evangelista's trade from the Nashville Predators to the New Jersey Devils could reshape his NHL future following a breakout season.
articles.body: One of the more notable early September trades in the NHL took place Tuesday when the Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils agreed to trade Luke Evangelista to New Jersey. The 24-year-old right winger is coming off his best NHL season, with 12 goals and 44 assists in 81 games.The deal gives the New Jersey Devils a young forward with NHL experience before the 2026-27 season. For the Nashville Predators, the return means more high-value draft assets and more flexibility to reshape the roster.Why did Nashville Predators trade Luke Evangelista to New Jersey Devils?Luke Evangelista, Nashville Predators to New Jersey Devils for a conditional 2028 first-round pick and New Jersey’s 2028 second-round pick. The first-round pick originally belonged to the Colorado Avalanche, and the terms could change Nashville’s compensation to Colorado’s 2029 first-round pick.Evangelista had a career year for the Nashville Predators, ending with 56 points on 12 goals and 44 assists in 81 games. It was a big step forward for the former second-round pick, who was taken 42nd overall by Nashville in 2020.He is in the last year of a two-year, $6 million deal that pays him $3 million per year on average. Evangelista can become a restricted free agent after the 2026-27 season, giving the Devils a full season to see if he’s a fit before a decision on his future has to be made.He thinks it wasn't an easy decision because Evangelista had become a fan favourite with the team's fans, Nashville Predators general manager Chris MacFarland said. But the organization viewed it as a way to gain roster and salary-cap flexibility and open spots for younger wingers.Nashville now has seven picks in the first two rounds of the next two drafts, giving the Predators more ammo for future trades, prospect and roster development.Why did Nashville Predators trade Luke Evangelista to New Jersey Devils?Evangelista provides another young forward option for the New Jersey Devils after a productive NHL season. His 56-point campaign provides the team with evidence that he can contribute offensively, and his age and contract situation give room for further development.The move also adds another player to New Jersey’s mix who can compete for an important forward role as the club prepares for the 2026-27 NHL season. articles.title: Tiger Woods pleads guilty to reckless driving, forfeits driving licence
articles.summary: Golfer’s driving licence will be suspended for five years under the terms of a plea agreement that dropped DUI charges.
articles.body:
Tiger Woods has entered a plea agreement to a reckless driving charge after a rollover crash in March near his home in Florida.

Woods appeared in a courtroom in Martin County on Wednesday and agreed to a reduced charge after he was initially charged with driving under the influence (DUI). A judge ordered his driving licence be suspended for five years.

Woods, 50, said little during the hearing and beforehand sat at the defence table, looking back at the courtroom gallery. He arrived at the courthouse with his girlfriend Vanessa Trump, President Donald Trump’s former daughter-in-law.

The golf legend previously pleaded not guilty to a driving under the influence charge. Woods was arrested after his SUV clipped a truck and rolled over on its side on a beachside residential road on Jupiter Island.

A sheriff’s report said deputies found two pain pills in his pocket and he showed signs of impairment. He did a breathalyser test, which came out negative, but refused to take a urine test.

Neither Woods nor the person in the other vehicle was injured in the crash, according to officials. But his Land Rover caused $5,000 in damage to the truck, according to a police report. Woods had told a deputy that he was looking down at his phone and changing the radio station when he hit the truck.

Woods is among the most influential figures in golf, but his career has been derailed by multiple back and knee surgeries, car crashes and a dependence on pain medication.

Woods has been involved in four crashes over the years. He took a leave from the golf tour after a 2009 crash and again after the latest crash and has yet to return to tournament play.

He left the United States to seek treatment at an inpatient treatment facility, according to court records.

Woods made his first public appearance since returning from treatment on June 23 when he introduced the PGA Tour’s plans to revamp its schedule for 2028. Woods remained as chairman of the tour’s Future Competition Committee after his arrest. He did not take questions during that appearance.

articles.summary: NHL News: Exploring Auston Matthews' unique leadership style and how it can influence the Toronto Maple Leafs under new head coach Jim Hiller, as the team aims for redemption in the 2026-27 NHL season.

articles.title: Throwback: Three years ago today, AEW fired CM Punk with cause after ugly backstage altercation
articles.summary: WWE News: Three years ago today, All Elite Wrestling (AEW) fired CM Punk with cause following a backstage incident involving Jack Perry at the All In pay-per-vi.
articles.body: Three years ago today, All Elite Wrestling (AEW) fired CM Punk with cause following a backstage incident involving Jack Perry at the All In pay-per-view at Wembley Stadium in London. The decision ended one of the most controversial runs in AEW history. Punk’s wrestling and employment contracts were terminated after an investigation into the altercation.The incident also involved AEW CEO Tony Khan. Reports said Punk confronted Khan and had to be restrained. Khan later said he felt his safety was in danger. The termination came after months of backstage tension and less than a year after Punk’s previous major confrontation with AEW executives and wrestlers.What happened when AEW fired CM Punk three years ago?The story goes back to August 27, 2023, when AEW presented All In at Wembley Stadium. It was one of the biggest shows in the company’s history. More than 80,000 fans were in attendance as AEW staged its first major event at the famous London venue.Punk was one of the central names on the card. He was also working in an environment that had already been affected by his previous backstage problems.The trouble reportedly began after Jack Perry’s match. Perry, the son of late actor Luke Perry, had been involved in a disagreement over the use of real glass during his match.Punk and Perry then got into a physical confrontation backstage. The incident quickly became more serious.Reports said Punk also confronted Tony Khan. The AEW boss later described the situation as frightening and said he believed his safety was at risk.To open AEW Collision several days later, Khan addressed the incident in a pretaped interview.“I’ve been going to wrestling shows for over 30 years. I’ve been producing them on this network for nearly four years. Never, in all that time, have I ever felt until last Sunday that my security, my safety, my life was in danger at a wrestling show. I don’t think anybody should feel that way at work”, Khan said on the show.AEW then investigated the incident. The company’s Discipline Committee met and later consulted outside legal counsel. The committee ultimately recommended that Punk be terminated with cause. Khan accepted the recommendation.“Following the investigation, the AEW Discipline Committee met and later convened with outside legal counsel before making a unanimous recommendation to [AEW owner Tony] Khan that CM Punk be terminated with cause,” AEW said in its statement.The firing was particularly significant because Punk had returned to AEW only months earlier. He had missed considerable time after suffering a torn biceps in a match in September 2022.That earlier period had also ended in controversy.Following the match, Punk delivered a heated news conference. He attacked several people connected to AEW and reportedly became involved in a physical confrontation with Matt Jackson, Nick Jackson and Kenny Omega.Punk’s history with AEW had already included tension with “Hangman” Adam Page and issues surrounding former friend Colt Cabana.By the time of the All In incident, the situation had reached another breaking point.Three years later, the firing remains one of the defining moments of AEW’s early history. Punk’s AEW run had begun with a huge reaction in Chicago in August 2021.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: El centrocampista portugués de 21 años causó sensación con su Peugeot Partner comercial
articles.body: Uno de los atractivos de los entrenamientos de los grandes equipos de fútbol es ver llegar a los jugadores en sus flamantes coches, especialmente en aquellos clubes en los que no tienen obligación contractual de llevar un modelo específico (normalemente patrocinador del club). Es el caso del Paris Saint Germain, una de cuyas estrellas se ha convertido en viral por el vehículo que llevó esta semana a una de las sesiones de Luis Enrique: el portugués Joao Neves. El centrocampista portugués, uno de los fijos del PSG al que este verano se vinculó en algunas ocasiones con el Real Madrid, ha dado mucho que hablar en redes sociales por la peculiar elección de coche para llegar a las instalaciones del Campus PSG, la ciudad deportiva del club galo situada a las afueras de París. Mientras que compañeros suyos como Kvaratskhelia lucen coches tan espectaculares como el Rolls-Royce Spectre (el primer modelo eléctrico de la firma británica está valorado en Francia en unos 350.000 euros como precio base), Neves optó por una... furgoneta en versión comercial. Aunque no se aprecia con claridad en las imágenes, MARCA ha podido saber que se trata de una Peugeot Partner BlueHDI de 102 CV (en todo esplendor comercial, hasta con llantas de chapa) con matrícula portuguesa, país natal del centrocampista. Si echamos un vistazo a la lista de precios de ese modelo en Francia, vemos que puede salir por unos 21.000 euros... dieciseis veces más barato que el Rolls del georgiano. No es la primera vez este verano que uno de los futbolistas del bicampeón de la Champions League llama la atención por lo contrario de lo habitual: la modestia de su elección de coche. Hace unas semanas fue Fabián Ruiz, el campeón del mundo con la selección española, el que sorrprendió a los aficionados que le esperaban en la puerta del entrenamiento llegando en un pequeño smart fortwo. Eso sí, en versión deportiva Brabus.

articles.title: Se hicieron pasar por su DT y cayó: la insólita estafa que sufrió José Enamorado en Brasil
articles.standfirst: Un estafador se hizo pasar por el técnico del Gremio y le quitó más de 13 millones de pesos al futbolista colombiano bajo el engaño de una falsa obra benéfica
articles.summary: Un estafador se hizo pasar por el técnico del Gremio y le quitó más de 13 millones de pesos al futbolista colombiano bajo el engaño de una falsa obra benéfica
articles.body: El fútbol brasileño ha sido escenario de una insólita y preocupante situación extrafutbolística que involucra al extremo colombiano José Enamorado, actual jugador del Gremio de Porto Alegre. El exjugador del Junior de Barranquilla fue víctima de un sofisticado engaño cibernético a través del cual perdió varios millones de pesos tras atender a una supuesta causa benéfica. El fraude comenzó cuando un delincuente logró suplantar la identidad del director técnico de Gremio, Luís Castro. Para ganar credibilidad y no levantar sospechas entre el plantel, el estafador entabló conversaciones continuas durante varios días con diferentes futbolistas. En esos chats analizaba partidos, discutía detalles tácticos y conversaba sobre el rendimiento en la cancha, imitando el estilo del estratega. Una vez construida la relación de confianza, el suplantador solicitó apoyo económico alegando que estaba organizando una labor social de carácter urgente y necesitaba contribuciones del equipo. Con la intención de colaborar con la causa de su entrenador, José Enamorado transfirió la suma de 22.000 reales brasileños (aproximadamente 13 millones de pesos colombianos). Tiempo después, al cruzar información en el entorno interno del club, se descubrió que el técnico jamás había enviado dichos mensajes ni solicitado el dinero. Al confirmarse la estafa masiva que afectó al colombiano y a otros integrantes del plantel, la directiva del club dio aviso inmediato a las autoridades. La Policía Civil de Río de Janeiro puso en marcha un operativo de rastreo denominado Operación 'Falso 9'. El operativo rindió frutos rápidamente. El sospechoso fue localizado en el municipio de Itaperuna, en el estado de Río de Janeiro. La captura se hizo efectiva en las primeras horas del martes 2 de septiembre de 2026. El detenido quedó a disposición de las autoridades judiciales brasileñas bajo cargos de delito de estafa y suplantación de identidad, con el fin de responder procesalmente y reembolsar los montos sustraídos. Este acontecimiento se suma a un ciclo desafiante para José Enamorado en el fútbol brasileño. Desde su vinculación a Gremio tras destacar en el Junior de Barranquilla, el atacante no ha logrado consolidarse del todo en el esquema titular. Debido a la irregularidad en sus participaciones y la exigencia del entorno de Porto Alegre, el extremo ha estado bajo el foco de las críticas por parte de la hinchada. A pesar del trago amargo fuera de las canchas, la rápida acción policial ofrece un parte de tranquilidad para que el jugador vuelva a enfocar sus esfuerzos en retomar su mejor nivel futbolístico.

articles.title: AEW's New Level Reveal WWE Pay Cut, New Rumors on Usos-Raw Censorship & Bronson Reed's Injury Rehab
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

New Level Reveal Info on WWE's Pay Cut Offer

The New Level provided some context this week to reports regarding WWE asking them to take a pay cut before they decided to depart the company.

During an appearance on the Ariel Helwani Show (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Kofi revealed that WWE's pay cut proposal was even more significant than originally believed, saying, "I don't know what's out there, but yeah, I will say it was more than 50 percent. A lot of people don't know it was more."

Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t Carrier ) reported in May that WWE was approaching some talent and asking them to take 50 percent pay cuts.

Because of that, it was assumed Kofi and Austin Creed were in that camp as well, but Kofi's comments suggest WWE wanted them to give up an even bigger piece of the pie.

Rather than accepting the proposal, Kofi and Creed turned it down and left WWE, ending their hugely successful tenures as Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods, known collectively as New Day.

On Sunday, Kofi and Creed made their AEW debuts as the New Level at All In, winning the AEW World Trios Championships with Swerve Strickland.

Appearing on TMZ Sports' Inside The Ring (h/t Derek Holloway of Ringside News), Kofi and Creed divulged that the freedom given to them to pursue outside projects played a major role in them choosing to sign with AEW.

"There's a lot of things in there that are very, I guess, player-friendly, right," Kofi said. "Like wrestler-friendly, you know, in terms of being able to go out and do what it is that you want to do.

"There's not really a lot of restriction. And that's really exciting, you know, to know that if you have a passion, you can go out there and follow it without worrying about, you know, someone telling you that you can't do it for whatever reason."

Creed added, "It's a crazy feeling because we have so many ideas and so many things that we want to do and try and see if we're good at. So to be able to have, I guess, like the gates kind of open to allowing that space in your brain to get out and stretch its legs some, I think is going to be really fulfilling."

While seeing Kofi and Creed leave WWE after more than a decade of immense success together was disappointing for some wrestling fans, they have already hit the ground running in AEW and appear poised to enjoy a great run there as well.

Reported Reason for Blood Censorship on Raw

Netflix reportedly made the call to censor blood during Monday night's pre-taped episode of WWE Raw.

According to False Finish , Netflix decided to pixelate the bloodshed that resulted from Royce Keys and OTM's attack of The Usos "due to restrictions in several countries where the show is broadcasted."

On last week's Raw, Keys and OTM interrupted the main event that pitted The Usos against LA Knight and Solo Sikoa by attacking all four Superstars.

This week's Raw opened with Keys and OTM jumping The Usos in the parking lot, but fans watching on Netflix did not get to experience the full effects of the assault due to the censorship.

However, WWE head of creative Triple H later posted the uncensored version of the segment on X:

There was another angle later in the show that saw Keys and OTM go after Sikoa, and the blood was censored on that occasion as well.

While Netflix's actions were a source of frustration for many fans, it doesn't figure to be a regular occurrence.

It is relatively rare for WWE to tape episodes of Raw and SmackDown ahead of time, so the opportunities for Netflix to review an episode and make those types of changes will be few and far between.

There is little that can be done in terms of censorship when Raw is live, and that is indeed the case the vast majority of the time.

Bronson Reed Reportedly Expected to Return Soon

Bronson Reed has been out of action since February, but his return reportedly may be on the horizon.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), Reed is now 100 percent healed from the torn biceps he suffered more than six months ago, and he is expected to be back on WWE programming within the next month.

Reed suffered the injury during a Triple Threat qualifying match for Elimination Chamber against Jey Uso and El Grande Americano.

All signs pointed toward Reed winning that match and then wreaking havoc in the chamber, but he was unable to continue due to the injury, and Uso came out on top.

Reed's injury came when Bron Breakker was already on the shelf, and although Breakker returned at WrestleMania, Logan Paul got injured in May.

The Vision has dealt with a string of bad injury luck, but with Reed's return on the horizon, the stable could be in line for a major shot in the arm.

At the same time, Reed's impending return could essentially serve as a reset or even a disintegration of the group should WWE decide to have him turn his back on The Vision and go off on his own.

articles.title: Aubameyang ‘humiliated’ as ex-Arsenal striker quits Gabon national team
articles.summary: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang cites 2025 Africa Cup of Nations treatment as captain steps away from Gabon duty.
articles.body:
Gabon captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has announced that he is stepping back from the national team, saying he felt “humiliated” by his exclusion and subsequent reinstatement after the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) in Morocco.

The top scorer in the history of the Panthers was singled out by the Gabonese government as responsible for the AFCON failure.

“They humiliated and smeared me even though I played at the AFCON while injured,” the 37-year-old said in a television interview.

“This is the last straw, and I’d rather stop here.”

Gabon were eliminated from the AFCON in the group stage after three defeats, the last of which came against Ivory Coast.

“It’s a part of our national identity that has been weakened,” Gabonese President Brice Oligui Nguema said at the time.

The government fired the coaching staff , suspended the team until further notice and sidelined Aubameyang and 38-year-old Bruno Ecuele Manga.

The suspension of these veteran mainstays of the squad sparked a wave of outrage among Gabonese supporters.

“I think the team’s problems run much deeper than the little person that I am,” said Aubameyang, who was one of Europe’s top strikers during his time at Borussia Dortmund and Arsenal.

The Gabonese striker has set himself what is likely to be a final challenge in Europe, leaving Marseille to join Deportivo La Coruna, who have just returned to La Liga after a long spell in the wilderness.

Gabon’s new national team coach, Sebastien Migne, will now have to plan without Aubameyang as he prepares his team for their first qualifiers later this month for next year’s AFCON.

Gabon are in Group A with World Cup quarter-finalists Morocco as well as Niger and Lesotho.

articles.body: El banquillo de Millonarios Fútbol Club vuelve a ser el epicentro de las miradas en el fútbol profesional colombiano. Tras la sorpresiva salida del entrenador argentino Fabián Bustos, la junta directiva de la institución capitalina se encuentra en la búsqueda urgente de un nuevo estratega que tome las riendas del equipo en pleno desarrollo de la Liga BetPlay. En medio de esta coyuntura, el nombre de un viejo y querido conocido ha cobrado una fuerza determinante: Alberto Gamero. La partida de Fabián Bustos dejó un vacío inesperado en el vestuario 'embajador'. A un día de disputar una nueva edición del clásico capitalino frente a Independiente Santa Fe, la dirección deportiva de Millonarios se vio obligada a mover sus fichas con celeridad. Mientras el entrenador Omar Rodríguez asumió de manera interina la conducción del plantel profesional para encarar el compromiso inmediato, las altas esferas del club iniciaron las evaluaciones para definir quién encabezará el proyecto deportivo en lo que resta del año. Alberto Gamero, de 62 años, se perfila como la opción más sólida para tomar la dirección técnica del equipo albiazul. Su regreso supondría el inicio de un segundo ciclo al frente de Millonarios, una institución que conoce a la perfección tanto en su etapa como futbolista como en su exitoso paso desde el banquillo técnico. Durante su primer ciclo como estratega, comprendido entre 2020 y finales de 2024, el 'Sonero' dejó huella en el fútbol capitalino: El resurgimiento del nombre de Gamero para Millonarios no es aislado; viene acompañado de un agitado panorama en el mercado de fichajes de entrenadores. Recientemente, el estratega samario estuvo en negociaciones avanzadas y cerca de concretar su vínculo con el Junior de Barranquilla. Sin embargo, las conversaciones tomaron un rumbo diferente en cuestión de horas —llevando al cuadro barranquillero a oficializar a Sebastián Viera en su banquillo—, coincidiendo con la vacante generada en la capital. Según reportes e informaciones preliminares del entorno del club, existen conversaciones y contactos entre la junta directiva y el entorno del DT para avanzar en los términos de su eventual vinculación. La afición permanece atenta a las definiciones oficiales en los próximos días, que determinarán si el técnico samario estampará su firma para liderar nuevamente las ilusiones del cuadro embajador. De acuerdo con información revelada por el periodista Mariano Olsen, Gamero se habría desplazado a Bogotá desde Panamá —donde participaba en el evento académico Fútbol 360 junto a estrategas como Reinaldo Rueda y Jaime De La Pava— para estar al pendiente de las negociaciones y concretar su posible regreso al club. Semanas antes de que se formalizara el despido de Bustos, Gamero fue consultado en una entrevista con el periodista Diego Rueda sobre la posibilidad de encarar un segundo ciclo al frente del cuadro 'Embajador'. El estratega samario dejó las puertas abiertas a un eventual retorno, argumentando que su salida anterior se dio en buenos términos. "Yo soy profesional. Yo en Millonarios no salí mal, ni peleando", afirmó Gamero al referirse a la opción de dirigir nuevamente en Bogotá. Además, remarcó el aprecio que mantiene por el club donde logró cosechar tres títulos locales (Liga, Copa Colombia y Superliga) entre 2020 y 2024: "Hay que valorar. Ir a una final es lo más importante; no es fácil jugar cinco finales", señaló al calificar su primer ciclo en la institución con una nota de "siete o siete y medio".

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Scott Pianowski shares his 'My Guys' — preferred players he's drafting often for 2026
articles.summary: The Sun God and King Henry highlight list of players Scott Pianowski loves for 2026 fantasy football.
articles.body:
I'm about 85% through my fantasy football drafts for 2026. The story isn't complete, but themes are taking shape. I now have a good sense of what players will define my 2026 season.

With so many drafts in the bank, it's a good time to roll through my preferred plays. You can call this piece "What's In My Wallet?" or "My Guys," it doesn't matter to me. I'm not hung up on labels.

Understand that player share counts will be significantly affected by some random things, like draft slot. If you're not continually gifted with the first overall pick, it's hard to be overweight on Jahmyr Gibbs. So it goes.

Any player considered in the first round carries a fun upside, but I also want to consider floor. The Sun God is as sturdy as they come, with an average return of 117-1,393-11.9 over the last three seasons. Tied to a plus quarterback, an easy schedule and a bunch of indoor games, I'm prepared to take St. Brown over Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Christian McCaffrey.

Brown is good at everything, a crafty runner, a handy receiver. The Bengals employ a narrow usage tree — the RB depth chart after Brown is uninspiring — and profile as a carnival team , yet again. Brown is a perfect second-round pick, and still in his prime entering his age-26 season.

I understand the surface concerns on Henry — he's a power back, he turned 32 in January, he's had a heavy career workload. But there's zero sign of attrition with The King. He's somehow improved in his two Baltimore seasons, pushing his YPC to 5.6 and scoring an absurd 34 touchdowns. And even if some efficiency drop creeps into his game this year, I suspect Henry would fall into the end zone 12-14 times even in a bad season. The Baltimore offense as a whole is an arrow pointing up, with new OC Declan Doyle providing a fresh coat of paint. When I don't land Brown in Round 2, I pivot to Henry when I can.

The dots line up so cleanly here. McConkey showed dominant potential in the second half of his rookie year, and the sophomore slump goes down as an excused absence — OL injuries, stale play-calling, crowded target tree. The line should be better this season — even with center Tyler Biadasz out for the year — and the WR room is leaner with Keenan Allen gone. And we can't underestimate the value of new OC Mike McDaniel, a creative, motion-heavy schemer who will put McConkey in spots to succeed. McConkey is a perfect fourth-round target.

I'm not going to dismiss Kyren Williams out of hand — I drafted him in the second round of the Yahoo Expert League on Tuesday — but Corum looms as a platoon partner. Corum entered the Circle of Trust for the final 11 games last year, producing at a clip that paces to 179-911-7.7 for a full season. Corum is another player you can draft at his floor, but still dream of a fun upside. The Rams should be a run-heavy team in the fourth quarter this year, with a loaded defense controlling outcomes on the other side.

Warren has carved out a solid NFL career after going undrafted four years ago. He'll cede a fair amount of work to new teammate Rico Dowdle, but there should be plenty of opportunity for both players. Warren's receiving chops (7.4 yards per target last year, 88.9% catch rate) are a perfect fit for veteran QB Aaron Rodgers, who is looking to dump the ball off as quickly as possible. No matter what your preferred RB strategy is, Warren is a pick that fits the build.

Quarterback is the no-stress position for fantasy football this summer, as deep as it's ever been. As a result, I'll skip the vanity options early and try to target some of the guys in this group. Every quarterback in this four-pack has a similar setup — an exciting collection of pass-catchers, and a defense that will likely force weekly shootouts. Carnival life for the win .

Loveland makes this list more in spirit than actual roster count, as I haven't quite acquired the commensurate shares I seek. But I can't unsee what he did at the end of 2025 (including playoffs), gobbling up 48 targets and posting a 28-378-2 line over his final four games. I'll check the FOMO box on Loveland in the next week, even if it means hitting that plus-one button aggressively in some salary cap drafts.

We went broke on the Minnesota offense last year, something I'm willing to blame mostly on overmatched QB J.J. McCarthy. Kevin O'Connell remains one of the sharpest coaches around, and whatever you think of QB Kyler Murray these days, he should be a notable upgrade over McCarthy. Mason is five years younger than Aaron Jones Sr., and was the more effective runner last year. Mason didn't quite pay off his sleeper tag last year, but I'm happy to double down. The Vikings should have plenty of positive game scripts, with star DC Brian Flores scheming up an above-average defense.

For a while this summer, Johnson was being drafted outside the top-20 tight ends on Yahoo, which never made sense. The market has come around since, in part because hotshot rookie WR Jordyn Tyson is down for a couple of months. But no matter the shape of this offense, Johnson (77-889-3 last year) is likely to be involved. It's no surprise he clicks so well with QB Tyler Shough, as the two players shared a season together at Oregon. Johnson is good enough to be a Week 1 starter in many fantasy leagues, and he's a dynamite backup TE in some other builds. He'll likely be my most rostered player this season.

Everyone has their own preferred list of one-injury-away running backs, the type of high-upside picks that make sense for stashing. Washington and Johnson played so well in the preseason that they might have a case for expanded roles in-season, and they're both behind backs with injury concerns (Ashton Jeanty is already dinged up, Kenneth Walker III has an extensive injury history). Davis won't have value unless James Cook (a terrific player) gets hurt, but at least Davis has already shown proof-of-concept on his upside. He exploded for 174 total yards against the Jets in January last year.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's takeaways from the Yahoo Fantasy Expert League Draft
articles.summary: Justin Boone breaks down the results from the recent Yahoo Fantasy Expert League draft.
articles.body:
The Yahoo Fantasy Expert League is officially underway! This is an actual league that we'll be competing in this season featuring 12 teams in a half-PPR format with the following roster spots: QB, RB, RB, WR, WR, WR, TE, FLEX, DEF, K, BN, BN, BN, BN, BN, IR, IR.

Let's dive into how it all played out over 15 rounds.

My Round 1 pick was the most controversial, but we'll get to that in a moment. The only other selection that went against the grain in the opening frame was St. Brown being taken ahead of Smith-Njigba. While that's not the way I'd play it, you can't really argue with the Sun God's consistency as a high-end producer. St. Brown has finished as a top-five fantasy wideout on a per game basis in three straight seasons.

My pick: I knew going into this draft that the top-two running backs would likely be off the board, forcing me to pick between an elite receiver (Chase, Nacua) or reach slightly for the next tier of running back. I was also well aware that in a draft with this crew of sharp analysts, RB values would be tough to come by later on. That led me to go against my rankings in this instance and take Taylor at 1.03. I've said this before, but rankings should be a guide to navigate your draft, not a list that you pick from without thinking. I'm higher than most on JT this season after he was the highest scoring fantasy back through 13 games last year while Daniel Jones was healthy. Getting him in this spot was important, since I'm expecting a major drop off at the position before my next pick at 2.09.

Running backs went off the board early and often here — as they should. The collection of Brown, Hampton, Walker, Achane, Henry and even Jeanty are strong Round 2 selections, regardless of the direction you went with your first pick. The only reason Jeanty fell to 2.08 is due to the questions about his early-season health, coming off the ankle injury in August. The one running back who was a bit of a surprise selection here was Williams, but Team Pianowski again chose a player with an excellent record of consistency. Williams has been a top-10 fantasy RB for three consecutive campaigns.

My pick: My fears about a massive run on RBs in the late first and early second came to fruition, with even Williams being added to that lengthy run. If Jeanty had made it just one more pick, he would have been the name I clicked here, since I'm not overly concerned about his injury status for Week 1. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case and I instead pivoted to my best player available in London. While some people seem concerned about the quarterback situation in Atlanta, let me remind you that London finished as the WR7 in fppg last year. Through 11 weeks, London was the third-highest scoring fantasy WR behind only JSN and Puka — and that was with Michael Penix Jr. serving as the starting QB.

The third round is where things started to get more interesting and strategies began to emerge. Etienne going off the board at the top of the third is a round earlier than his ADP, but I recently made the case for him as an important fantasy target. If you're planning to take a running back in this range, you have to accept that they come with more risk than the top 12 at the position. That's why most managers elected to take receivers, while Team Loeb broke the quarterback seal. Allen is an amazing fantasy asset, but even as a Bills fan I can admit that it's tough to justify a QB this early when there's so much depth at the position. Keep Allen at the 3.07 spot in mind when we discuss some of the QB values in later rounds.

My pick: I considered Javonte Williams here, but ultimately went with Olave. We're starting three receivers in this league and Olave gives me a chance to field two of the top-10 players at the position. He finished as the WR9 in fppg last season, while averaging the sixth-most targets per outing in Kellen Moore's fast-paced offense. We also saw the best version of Olave down the stretch, when he was the second-highest scoring wideout in the fantasy playoffs. Rookie Jordyn Tyson will miss time in the first half of the season, setting Olave up for monster volume once again.

With the current RB landscape, you can make a strong argument for Breece Hall and D'Andre Swift as third-round values. So, seeing them slip to the early fourth round was rough knowing they wouldn't get back to me at the end of the frame. Team Norris is the only roster with three backs through four rounds and it's going to form an impressive core for his starting lineup. However, he's also one of two squads that only has a single receiver so far. The other is Team Loeb, who put himself in a very difficult build with only one RB and one WR in his first four picks. He's facing an uphill battle the rest of the way, given the expected cliff coming at running back and the format featuring three wideouts in the starting lineup.

My pick: I wasn't in love with the value of the RBs in this range and knew I could get one of my WR targets with a future pick, so I spent up on a potential elite TE in Loveland. Though his 713 yards and six touchdowns made for a solid rookie year, his real upside emerged in the second half of the season, when he was the TE5 overall over the final nine weeks. The 22-year-old became a focal point of the Bears' passing attack over his last four outings (including playoffs), posting stat lines of 6-94-1, 10-91-1, 8-137-0 and 4-56-0 — while earning at least 10 targets in each of those contests.

It was a mixed bag in Round 5, with players going off the board at every position. Team Allen getting Jackson as his QB two rounds after Allen is nice value for a player with an equally high ceiling. Team Harmon grabbing a potential elite TE in Warren at 5.08 was one of my favorite picks in this draft. Receivers tend to be my most frequent target in this area, but Round 5 is often the last train out of the station for anyone in search of guaranteed RB volume mixed with upside. Irving, Judkins, Montgomery and Tuten come with red flags (which is why they are fifth-round picks), but all four are solid low-end RB2 options.

My pick: Can you believe I didn't take a running back with this pick? Though I debated scooping up Judkins or Montgomery in this spot, I decided to secure my third receiver in Watson. There will be a few intriguing wideouts selected in the next couple rounds, but Watson showed us what he's capable of last year when he was the WR16 in fppg while suiting up 10 games. I expect the Packers to increase their pass volume this season, while featuring a more condensed receiver depth chart. A healthy Watson has top-12 potential at his position, thanks to his big-play ability and TD scoring.

While the quality of running backs available in Round 6 has declined, the panic is setting in for managers who haven't secured enough talent at the position. If that's not a scenario you want to find yourself in, then make sure you have two or possibly three running backs through the first five frames. There is a flip side to that coin though. Team Norris is on a wild ride that's only resulted in one receiver through the first six rounds. If he can hit on some receivers moving forward, his roster will be tough to beat. But that's a big IF at this point in the draft.

My pick: Even knowing how running-back hungry the Yahoo analysts would be in this draft, I wasn't willing to overpay for my RB2 in the early rounds. Now that I have a solid Hero RB base for my lineup, I will take a shot on a boom-or-bust back in Lloyd. Josh Jacobs' situation is completely up in the air and could play out in many ways. The path that seems most likely to me is Lloyd opening the season as the Packers' starter, with a chance to establish himself as the lead back moving forward — if Jacobs doesn't return. Lloyd has impressed this summer, while finally staying healthy for an extended stretch. Whether he can keep that up during the season remains to be seen, but it's worth noting that he spent months working with the Meyer Institute of Sport in California this offseason in an attempt to solve his durability issues.

It's easy to question the potential for something when we've never seen it happen before, but in the sixth round I'm willing to take a chance on an explosive back who could be on the verge of a breakout.

Round 7 still has plenty of interesting players who could vastly outproduce their draft slots, especially at receiver. Harrison hasn't been as bad as the public perception would have you believe, Tate is an exciting rookie who needs to overcome a bad offense, Sutton always has TD upside, Pierce could be a fantasy WR2 if he gets back to 100%, Wilson is hoping to maintain his late-season momentum, Metcalf is a big-play waiting to happen and Godwin might be the Bucs' No. 1 WR early in the season while his teammates recover from injury. All seven of those wideouts can be solid fantasy WR3/flex options.

My pick: With most of my starting lineup filled out and no tight end or running back values catching my eye here, I took the fifth quarterback in this draft and someone whom I believe can challenge for QB1 overall status in 2026. Hurts is learning a different offense and getting used to some new teammates, but in a four-point passing touchdown league his rushing upside makes him more valuable. Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has made it clear that the Tush Push isn't going away and Hurts will benefit from the easiest fantasy QB schedule that begins with the Commanders and Titans. As long as his offensive line stays healthy, Hurts will be a difference-maker in this league.

We've entered "Get Your Guys" territory, where managers should be filling out their rosters with the players they believe could vastly outproduce this draft slot. I was hoping to get Stribling or one of the running backs here (Croskey-Merritt, Mason, Dowdle), but other managers wisely scooped them up before I got back on the clock. Stribling is the exact kind of receiver that could turn Team Norris into a juggernaut if he hits. He's managed to backfill his WR room with Higgins, Metcalf and Stribling — and he's not done yet.

My pick: With all those names I mentioned above flying off the board before my pick, it left me in a spot where there were no values I wanted to draft at RB or WR. Instead, I took a different approach and chose a player I know will be more valuable than an eighth round pick in Kittle. We still don't know if Kittle will be active for the 49ers' opener in Australia (he's traveling with the team), but it's possible. If he sits out, we'll almost surely see him in Week 2. Let me remind everyone, Kittle has finished as a top-three fantasy TE in per game scoring seven of the last eight years. You don't win your league in the draft, you win it by drafting well and then managing your roster during the season. Kittle now gives me some trade options down the road. If he returns to form, I could deal Kittle or Loveland away for an upgrade elsewhere in my lineup. Though it's unconventional and takes some imagination, I will turn one of these tight ends into a quality RB or WR starter.

Quarterbacks have started to get selected more frequently in the last few rounds, with Prescott and Herbert joining the party in this frame. Being able to get a player like Prescott, who was the QB7 last year averaging 20.2 fppg in the ninth round, makes taking Allen (QB1 with 23.4 fppg) in Round 3 hard to justify. Herbert also has top-five upside with Mike McDaniel taking over as the Chargers OC.

My pick: Part of me wishes I had taken Jacobs here to guarantee I would have the Packers' starting running back no matter what happens. However, there were still too many useful options to roll the dice on a player who might not play at all in 2026. Instead I went with Gainwell, who is an underrated asset capable of offering weekly RB3/flex value as the Buccaneers' 1B back next to Irving. We also saw Gainwell's potential in Pittsburgh last year. In the four games where Gainwell saw at least 15 touches for the Steelers, he posted 134 yards and two TDs in the first, 105 yards in the second, 122 yards in the third and 126 yards in the fourth. If Irving misses time again, Gainwell will immediately be in the conversation as a top-15 fantasy back.

As much as it pains me to write it, Team Norris and Team Loeb did a good job filling out their receiver depth charts in the middle rounds. Norris ended up with Higgins, Metcalf, Stribling, Pittman and Diggs, while Loeb got Adams, Odunze, Pierce and Lemon. The bigger concern for Team Loeb will be his RB2 spot (Warren/JCM), so he'll likely be battling with me for the early-season waiver wire backs that emerge.

My pick: It's unknown when Tyson will return from his latest hamstring injury, but it won't be before October. The summer reports out of New Orleans were emphatic enough about his potential that even if he misses the first half of the season, I want him on my roster when he does return. This also insulates me against an injury to Olave at some point during the year. I can also stash Tyson away on IR for the opening month and pick up another late-round bench stash of waivers.

articles.title: Revelan desde Portugal la razón oculta por la que Richard Ríos fichó por el Al-Ittihad
articles.standfirst: Destapan el verdadero motivo por el que Richard Ríos prefirió la oferta millonaria del Al-Ittihad
articles.summary: Destapan el verdadero motivo por el que Richard Ríos prefirió la oferta millonaria del Al-Ittihad
articles.body: El mercado de pases del fútbol internacional suele entregar giros inesperados en sus últimas horas, y el caso del volante colombiano Richard Ríos se ha convertido en una de las historias más destacadas del periodo de transferencias de 2026. Tras apenas una temporada vistiendo la camiseta del Benfica de Portugal, el mediocampista de 26 años ha definido su salida en calidad de préstamo hacia el Al-Ittihad de la Liga Profesional Saudí. Lo que parecía un destino improbable para un jugador que venía en franco ascenso terminó concretándose debido a factores clave destapados por la propia prensa portuguesa, particularmente por diarios como A Bola. A pesar de haber firmado una notable campaña inicial con el Benfica en la temporada 2025-2026 —sumando más de 45 partidos disputados, ocho goles y seis asistencias—, la realidad futbolística de Ríos dentro del esquema técnico cambió drásticamente para el arranque de la nueva competencia. El volante antioqueño comenzó a perder terreno en la alineación titular, relegado al banquillo tras incorporaciones tácticas en el medio campo de Las Águilas. Ante la falta de minutos garantizados y la decisión de la directiva lusa de ubicarlo en la lista de jugadores negociables para aligerar la masa salarial, el colombiano y sus agentes comenzaron a explorar alternativas en el cierre de la ventana de pases. De acuerdo con lo revelado por los medios de comunicación lusitanos, la principal motivación detrás de la elección del colombiano no fue únicamente la búsqueda de continuidad en el terreno de juego, sino las condiciones financieras impuestas en la oferta de Yeda. La prensa lusa detalló que la directiva del Al-Ittihad realizó un esfuerzo económico sustancial para amarrar la cesión del mediocampista de la Selección Colombia: El conjunto árabe acordó el pago de un cargo de cesión (tasa de préstamo) que ronda entre los tres y cuatro millones de euros a las arcas del Benfica. Al-Ittihad asumirá la totalidad de la ficha contractual de Ríos, garantizándole un salario sustancialmente superior al que percibía en el fútbol europeo. El contrato de cesión se firmó por un año (hasta mediados de 2027) sin opción de compra implícita, lo que le permite al Benfica mantener los derechos federativos del futbolista para una hipotética venta futura o su eventual retorno a Europa. Por el lado del fútbol saudí, la llegada de Richard Ríos respondió a una urgencia táctica en las últimas 48 horas del mercado. Tras truncarse las conversaciones entre el club de Yeda y el Benfica por el fichaje del luxemburgués Leandro Barreiro por discrepancias en las formas de pago, las directivas de los 'Tigres' activaron de inmediato la alternativa del colombiano. En Medio Oriente, los medios locales ya catalogan a Ríos como la "pieza faltante" en la medular del equipo. En el Al-Ittihad compartirá vestuario con figuras internacionales de la talla de Steven Bergwijn, Houssem Aouar y Danilo Pereira, buscando devolver al equipo a los puestos de vanguardia de la liga saudí. Con este movimiento, Ríos hace una pausa temporal en su ciclo en el balompié del viejo continente para encarar un reto donde la exigencia económica y el protagonismo inmediato fueron los grandes argumentos que inclinaron la balanza a favor del gigante árabe.

articles.title: El Rayo niega presiones de Presa a los técnicos de la CAM en la visita a Vallecas
articles.standfirst: El club sostiene que el presidente pidió identificar a los técnicos y reunió a las empresas mantenedoras para facilitar la inspección. La Comunidad mantiene que la decisión final depende del auditor
articles.summary: El club sostiene que el presidente pidió identificar a los técnicos y reunió a las empresas mantenedoras para facilitar la inspección. La Comunidad mantiene que la decisión final depende del auditor
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano niega de manera rotunda que Raúl Martín Presa ejerciera supuestas presiones sobre los técnicos de la Comunidad de Madrid durante la visita realizada al estadio de Vallecas. El club asegura que la inspección estaba programada y que el presidente se limitó a pedir que los técnicos se identificasen, comprobando que eran los mismos que ya habían acudido al recinto el pasado mes de diciembre. Desde la entidad franjirroja explican que, con el objetivo de facilitar toda la información requerida, Presa llamó a los responsables de las empresas mantenedoras para que formasen parte de la visita. La intención era que pudieran resolver sobre el terreno cualquier cuestión técnica relacionada con el estado del estadio. El club sí reconoce que, en ese espacio de tiempo, el presidente estuvo reunido con los técnicos de la CAM. Durante ese encuentro, Presa les trasladó la importancia que tiene para la entidad poder jugar en Vallecas este sábado y la necesidad de actuar con celeridad en los plazos, pero el Rayo rechaza que aquello pueda interpretarse como una presión. La entidad sostiene que, una vez revisado todo lo requerido, los técnicos concluyeron que el estadio estaba en condiciones para acoger el encuentro. Esa valoración fue trasladada también a Óscar Valentín, capitán del equipo, que estuvo presente durante la visita. El Rayo recuerda además que la semana pasada ya acudieron al estadio otros técnicos de la Comunidad de Madrid. En aquella visita, según explican desde el club, se trasladó la necesidad de modificar una serie de bombillas y un cable. Esas actuaciones fueron realizadas esa misma tarde, por lo que la entidad entiende que los requerimientos señalados quedaron subsanados de forma inmediata. En Vallecas consideran que esos trabajos, unidos a la revisión de este miércoles, refuerzan su postura de que el estadio está preparado para recibir de nuevo a la afición franjirroja. El club insiste en que el regreso a su campo es una cuestión prioritaria y que no existe ningún inconveniente técnico para disputar allí el partido del sábado. La Comunidad de Madrid, por su parte, mantiene su versión y rebaja el alcance de la valoración de los técnicos desplazados al estadio. Desde la CAM insisten en que esos técnicos no tienen capacidad de decisión definitiva y que, aunque el informe pueda ser positivo, será el auditor el que tenga que concluir oficialmente si el estadio está apto. Hasta entonces, el Rayo se mantiene a la espera de una resolución definitiva por parte de la Comunidad de Madrid, mientras defiende que la visita técnica ha confirmado que Vallecas está en condiciones para que se pueda jugar este sábado.

articles.title: Emil Morales & recent history of Dodgers minor league 100-RBI seasons
articles.summary: This is the final week of the regular season for both Class-A and High-A, and both Great Lakes and Ontario have a pair of standout players in one specific ar...
articles.body:
This is the final week of the regular season for both Class-A and High-A , and both Great Lakes and Ontario have a pair of standout players in one specific area.

Shortstop Emil Morales began the season in Ontario before getting promoted to Great Lakes in May , and he hasn't stopped hitting. Morales has rocketed up prospect lists, including getting rated 29th overall by Baseball America in August . Between the two levels, Morales has driven in 115 runs in 113 games, and doesn't turn 20 until September 22.

In the last 50 years, only four other Dodgers minor leaguers had at least 100 RBI in their age-19 season or younger — Mike Marshall (1979), Candy Maldonado (1980), Adrían Beltré (age 18 in 1997), and Cody Bellinger ( 2015 ).

Ontario first baseman and occasional third baseman Easton Shelton has 35 home runs this year, 15 more than any other player in the circuit. The 20-year-old Shelton has driven in 106 runs in 106 games this season. We'll know by Sunday if Morales or Shelton can be the first Dodgers minor leaguers with at least 100 RBI and as many runs batted in as games played since Greg Brock knocked in 138 runs in 135 games for Triple-A Albuquerque in 1982.

In the last 50 years, the only other Dodgers minor leaguers with 100 RBI and at least as many RBI as games are Kelly Snider (139 RBI in 138 games for Class-A Lodi in 1977) and Mike Marshall (137 RBI in 128 games while inning Pacific Coast League MVP for Albuquerque in 1981).

Josue De Paula, the Dodgers top prospect, has a chance to join this group, as he's sitting on 99 RBI with 11 more games left in Double-A Tulsa's season. The last Tulsa Driller to knock in 100 runs was Joe Koshansky in 2006 when Tulsa was a Colorado Rockies affiliate. De Paula has already scored 100 runs this season, and if he drives home another run will be just the second Tulsa Drillers player with triple digits in both runs and RBI since then-Rangers prospect Carlos Peña in 2000.

James Tibbs III, who was not called up to the Dodgers , is also sitting on 96 RBI for Oklahoma City with nearly three weeks to go in the Pacific Coast League season, so he could easily join this group, too.
