articles.title: Raiders optimistic Ashton Jeanty will be ready to play in Week 1
articles.summary: News not so great for rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford
articles.body:
While the Las Vegas Raiders' big news of Wednesday was coach Klint Kubiak naming veteran Kirk Cousins the starting quarterback over No. 1 overall pick, Rookie Fernando Mendoza, there was other significant news offered by the coach that also affects the Week 1 season opener against Miami Dolphins on Sept 13.

Asked if he is optimistic that starting running back Ashton Jeanty will be ready for the opener that looms in 11 days, Kubiak simply said "yes."

Tuesday, Las Vegas Raiders general John Spytek said this of Jeanty's return from injury : "I expect him to be back as quick as he can," Spytek said. "Maybe quicker than some would expect, but we'll see.'

Jeanty was working on the side Tuesday with a trainer as he recovers from suffering an ankle injury 10 days ago. He has not practice since the injury. Clearly, the team is hopeful he will be able to work next week prior to the Miami game. This is continued good news after the team was initially worried Jeanty suffered a serious injury.

Meanwhile, the injury news isn't as good regarding rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford. Kubiak said the third-round pick, who was put on the season-ending injured reserve Sunday, suffered an Achilles injury. Thursday night, the team said it was ankle injury.

That is an important clarification because Achilles injury timelines are usually much longer than ankle injuries. Potentially, this injury could affect whether Crawford is ready for training camp next year.

Meanwhile, Kubiak didn't say whether Jackson Powers-Johnson or Caleb Rogers will start at right guard. He said they're both starters and they both will play this season. Powers-Johnson has been working with the first-team offense mostly lately.

Rookie running back Mike Washington is now wearing No. 4 and kicker Matt Gay is wearing No. 14.

articles.title: Tiger Woods banned from driving for 5 years as part of DUI plea deal
articles.summary: Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to reduced charges of reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test on Wednesday, Sept. 2, in a plea deal.
articles.body:
Professional golfer Tiger Woods pleaded no contest to reduced charges of reckless driving and refusal to submit to a lawful test on Wednesday, Sept. 2, in a plea deal in his DUI case in Martin County Circuit Court in Florida.

Woods' driver's license was suspended for five years as part of the agreement, and he agreed to pay $1,500 in fines.

Woods' SUV collided with a trailer being hauled by a truck on a busy Florida roadway on March 27, causing his vehicle to roll onto its side.

Woods told police responding at the scene that he had looked down at his phone and adjusted his radio, failing to see the vehicle in front of him slowing down.

But officers at the scene said Woods was "sweating profusely," according to an arrest affidavit.

Woods failed several sobriety tests at the scene, according to the arrest affidavit. Responding officers also found two hydrocodone pills in his pocket after the crash.

'No exceptions' to suspended license for Tiger Woods

Judge Darren Steele said there were "no exceptions" to the driving ban for five years for Woods.

"Sir, I want you to understand that five years of driving is for the safety of the public. There are no exceptions," he said. "If you were to drive for any reason at all, you would go immediately back to jail."

Woods hasn't competed on the PGA Tour since July 2024.

articles.title: Thousands including Geraint the dog cheer on Tour of Britain cyclists
articles.summary: The first stage started, and ended, in Lincoln, with supporters describing the event as "amazing".
articles.body:
The first stage of the 2026 Tour of Britain men's cycling race started in Lincolnshire earlier.

Riders set off from Lincoln and raced through towns and villages including Market Rasen, Rothwell, Caistor, Waddingham and Burton before returning to the city centre.

They covered a total of about 113.4 miles (182.5km) with an elevation of 4,570ft (1,393m).

According to Lincolnshire County Council, about 8,000 spectators turned out to cheer the competitors in Lincoln, with mini events and celebrations held along the route.

The race began with a neutralised start at Castle Square, where riders travelled through the opening section at a controlled speed before the official racing got under way on Wragby Road at about 10:45 BST.

Hundreds of people also stayed to watch the race at the tour village at Lincoln Castle.

Cycling enthusiast Grey Gilbey said: "I think it's fantastic. Lincoln has got a huge history of cycling events and we've got the iconic Michaelgate.

"It's good for the area, its good for the region and for the businesses, but it's also a good lift at the end of the summer, as well."

Alexei, 10, said: "There are quite a lot of crowds. To see it, you have to push through a bit."

Ada, also 10, added: "It was quite exciting. I was holding a sign so my mum had to hold the cowbells."

Along the route on the way out of the city centre, Geraint the dog, who is named after cyclist Geraint Thomas, was among those cheering on the riders with his owners.

Richard Rushby said: "We've loved coming to watch this. We've seen the Tour de France five times, so it's fantastic."

After making their way out of the city centre, the peloton then headed out into the Lincolnshire Wolds towards Market Rasen.

Councillor Stephen Bunney said: "It's a boost for everybody in the town.

"To get a national event here just gives that great lift up to what we are here in rural Lincolnshire."

Organisations such as community space Grange Hub Cafe celebrated the occasion by decorating bikes and holding an event for customers.

Supervisor and local councillor Alison Kitchin said she hoped the event would help showcase what the town had to offer.

"It's massive for the whole area, for the Wolds, not just for Market Rasen. Hopefully, everyone else will be embracing them."

Hundreds lined the streets of Caistor, where the town had been preparing in advance to welcome the cyclists.

Volunteers had hosted a competition for the best cycling-themed shop, home or garden display, which was decided by TV personality and former motorbike racer Guy Martin.

About 40 donated bikes painted in the colours of the county's flag were also placed along the route, with Lincolnshire-themed treats and live music keeping crowds entertained.

Jim Togher, who organised a lot of the celebrations, said he was "elated" and "emotional".

"Watching the race come through and [seeing] everybody that excited, kids screaming and cowbells and whistles... it was amazing," he added.

After the cyclists had gone past, David Wildman added that his "heart was still pumping from watching them".

"They came past so fast, it was like a blur," he said.

Residents lined the streets in Burton village as the cyclists whizzed past as part of five laps around Lincoln at the end of the race.

South Carlton District Peddlers had ridden to see the first part at North Willingham, and then stopped off in Burton to watch at a later stage.

Sarah Buckley said: "It's just such a whoosh when they come past, the whole lot of them. It's just amazing."

As part of each of the final five laps of the city, cyclists had to ride up Michaelgate - a cobbled street with a gradient of up to 20%.

Sue Frost was watching from behind the barrier with her family and friends, and said she had cycled up the gruelling hill several times in the past.

"The burn is in your chest and your heart feels like it's right up here in your throat. It's a great feeling.

"It's great to see it in Lincoln, it's fabulous for the city to see people going up on the cobbles. It's brought loads of people out, and thank goodness the rain has held off!"

British cyclist Lewis Askey, who rides for the NSN Cycling Team, won the first stage of the race.

The second stage will officially get under way in Boston tomorrow, at about 10:45.

articles.title: Bold prediction for 2026 Colts revolves around WR Josh Downs
articles.summary: Dan Graziano's bold prediction for the 2026 Indianapolis Colts centers around WR Josh Downs.
articles.body:
Ahead of the 2026 regular season starting, ESPN's Dan Graziano put together his bold but realistic predictions for each NFL team. His prediction for the Indianapolis Colts centered around wide receiver Josh Downs.

In an offense that features Alec Pierce's big-play ability and Tyler Warren's high-level production from the tight end position, Graziano believes that Downs can lead the team in receiving this season.

Graziano writes that with Pierce sidelined during training camp, the team was unable to implement his expanded role within the offense. He also points out that with Michael Pittman and his 110 targets from the 2026 season now in Pittsburgh, there will be more opportunities available for Downs.

The early expectation this season is that Downs will see more opportunities to line up outside as well, creating more chances to get the ball on intermediate and downfield routes, potentially leading to more production.

In terms of raw production last season, Downs took a step back, but he still remained an efficient target and a go-to option for Daniel Jones on third downs.

Throughout the offseason, the Colts have remained bullish on Downs' ability to make a big impact this season.

"I think getting lost in this a little bit is ... Josh Downs," GM Chris Ballard said earlier this offseason, via ESPN's Stephen Holder . "I think Josh Downs is freaking good. I do. I've always thought he's good. I think allowing him some more opportunities, we're going to see some of the special stuff you've seen in the past, but more."

articles.title: 'He's earned it': Why Raiders named Kirk Cousins starting QB
articles.summary: In a much-anticipated decision, the Las Vegas Raiders did the expected and named Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback for Week 1.
articles.body:
In a much-anticipated decision, the Las Vegas Raiders named Kirk Cousins their starting quarterback for Week 1.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak announced the news Wednesday, Sept. 2.

"He played really good football," Kubiak said, via the team's official website. "I'm really happy with all three of our quarterbacks. Kirk's had a really good offseason, very good camp and he's earned it."

Cousins will start the Raiders' season opener against the Miami Dolphins in Las Vegas.

"Where I've seen him grow is in his leadership and his command," Kubiak said of Cousins.

No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and Aidan O'Connell will be the Raiders' backup quarterbacks.

From Andy Reid to a 36-year-old rookie, NFL head coaches ranked by age

Why Raiders decided to start Kirk Cousins over Fernando Mendoza

Cousins' placement atop Las Vegas' quarterback depth chart was long expected despite the Raiders selection of Mendoza with the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Raiders brass have specified their intention to take a conservative approach with Mendoza as he transitions to the NFL. Kubiak said Raiders co-owner Tom Brady was involved in the decision.

"We lean on him for a lot of things. Talk to him multiple times a week. He's been extremely helpful for roster building, for schematics, for team building," Kubiak told reporters. "He's been an extremely impressive resource."

Mendoza showed some rookie growing pains during the preseason . The Indiana product completed 25 of 45 passes for 240 yards to go with one touchdown and two interceptions. Mendoza had some positive moments, but the speed of the game and some defensive coverages gave him trouble.

The Raiders decision to start Cousins is about comfort and familiarity to begin the season. Cousins knows Kubiak well from their days together in Minnesota. Kubiak was the Vikings quarterback coach (2019–2020) and offensive coordinator (2021) when Cousins was Minnesota's QB1.

The Raiders signed Cousins this offseason with the idea that he'll be a bridge quarterback and mentor. The Raiders' decision underscores they are moving forward with that plan.

articles.title: How Lil Wayne's son, Dwayne Carter III, is carving a path of his own
articles.summary: Dwayne Carter III has spent his life around the spotlight, but football is giving him a chance to create one of his own.
articles.body:
When Gainesville (Ga.) kicker Dwayne Carter III stepped onto the field to attempt his first field goal against No. 7 Buford on national television, he wasn't nervous.

Carter, the son of five-time Grammy Award-winning rapper Lil Wayne, knew what it felt like to have the spotlight on him.

The cameras weren't following him because of his father; they were following him because of what he had done himself.

"Obviously, there have been cameras in my face growing up for different things, but this was like a whole different thing," Carter said. "It was really exciting because they were talking about me for the reason I wanted to be talked about. They were highlighting what I've been working at and that it's paying off."

Carter, who transferred to Gainesville from North Atlanta ahead of his senior season, was 2-for-2 on his field goal attempts in the Red Elephants' 39-19 loss to the Wolves on Saturday, Aug. 22. His first gave them a 3-0 lead over the reigning GHSA Class 6A state champions.

While Carter's two younger brothers are following in their father's footsteps in the music industry, he always knew he wanted to take a different path.

"I've been very into sports," Carter said. "My dad knows that and my brothers know that. They always support me with my sports and they're always behind me on that."

That doesn't mean Carter has stayed completely away from music.

"When we're just kind of hanging out and stuff as a brother thing, I will make music with them just as a family bonding experience," he said.

His own path in sports began with soccer. But after repeatedly asking to play football, Carter's mom, Sarah Vivan, eventually agreed to let him put on a helmet and pads as a sophomore in high school.

"Football can get a little crazy; it can get a little violent," Vivan said. "I really just didn't want him having concussions or head injuries. But eventually, I understood the passion in wanting to play. So I just kind of did a compromise. 'If you can promise me you'll try being a kicker, then I'll be OK with you playing.'"

Now, it's pretty clear from watching Vivan in the stands that she's more than OK with it.

"I am one of those, dare I say, embarrassing moms who likes to coach and yell on the side," Vivan said.

"He said yesterday – I didn't know this – but after each kick, he looks for me in the crowd to see my reaction."

"If it's a good kick, she just kind of gives me a smile and like a little head nod," Carter said.

articles.title: NWSL Matchweek 19 Top 8 Moments
articles.summary: Fun comebacks, and huge wins highlight the NWSL weekend
articles.body:
1. Trinity Byars bags a brace once again in Wave 3-2 win against Racing Louisville

San Diego Wave were down 2-0 at home against Racing Louisville. The visiting side conceded possession, but were ready for their few moments they had with a goal against the run of play, and a set piece. However, San Diego did not waiver keeping the pressure high and earning a 3-2 comeback win in the second half with a brace a brace by Trinity Byars and a game-winning goal from the returning Kenza Dali. The brace was Byars' second in a row, and kept the Wave into fourth place on the NWSL table.

2. Paige Metayer scores her first goal of the NWSL season in Spirit win over Bay FC

The Washington Spirit were on a four-match winless streak heading into the weekend against Bay FC, but turned the results around with an important 1-0 win against Bay FC. The lone goal for the Spirit came at the end of stoppage time when Trinity Rodman used her patented speed to get down the pitch and into a dangerous position inside the penalty area. Rodman didn't have a clear look on goal so she crossed it to the middle for Paige Metayer who only needed to touch it to make it 1-0.

3. Gotham FC and Portland Thorns play to draw in potential playoff preview

The Portland Thorns proved once again they can keep up with a top team like Gotham FC, and Gotham extended their undefeated streak to 10 matches with their last loss on the road against San Diego Wave FC on July 4.

The best moment of the night came from an unbelievable goal by Jaedyn Shaw that had many debating whether it was intended to be a cross or a shot. Ultimately the Thorns responded after the referee determined Jaelin Howell conceded a penalty following a VAR review.

4. Denver Summit offense explodes in 6-1 victory against the Chicago Stars

Many teams have beaten the Chicago Stars this season, but Denver Summit made a huge impact scoring six goals over the course of 90 minutes for their largest win in the club's short history. Five different players got on the scoresheet: Janine Sonis, Olivia Thomas, Yuzuki Yamamoto, Tash Flint, and Melissa Kössler who scored a brace.

Olivia Thomas' goal was the final goal of the night and the first goal of her professional career. The victory put the Summit within four points of the final spot in the NWSL playoffs.

5. Angel City FC notch five in Monday night football match against Boston Legacy

Angel City FC ended a six-match winless streak with their 5-2 win against Boston Legacy in what could be the start of another Los Angeles versus Boston sports rivalry. The win put the Southern California club into 9th place and only two points out of the final playoff spot in the NWSL. As noted by OptaJack Angel City became the first-ever NWSL team to score three goals from outside the penalty area in a regular-season match.

6. Utah Royals send Pride coach packing in 2-1 win

The Orlando Pride decided to fire Head Coach Seb Hines following a thus far underwhelming 2026 season. The straw that broke the camel's back was their 2-1 loss against the Utah Royals. The Pride took the lead before the end of the first half, but allowed the Royals to control the game with their possession and create two goals in the second half. Cloe Lacasse was involved in both goals, first scoring the equalizer then getting the assist later on.

7. Kansas City Current hold off Courage in 3-2 victory at CPKC stadium

Ashley Sanchez bagged a brace in each of her last two matches with the Courage, but Kansas City was able to slow down the NWLS Golden Boot leader in a 3-2 victory in CPKC Stadium. The Current scored all their goals in the first half which included an incredible goal toward the near post by Croix Bethune.

8. Maddie Dahlien puts Seattle Reign ahead with 1-0 win against Houston Dash

The Seattle Reign kept the final spot in the NWSL playoffs with nine matches left in their season with a 1-0 win against the Houston Dash. The lone goal of the night came just a few minutes after play restarted in the second half around the 52nd minute. Reign 's leading scorer, Maddie Mercado moved the ball down the pitch drawing defenders leaving Maddie Dahlien wide open for a cross from Mercado to score easily making it 1-0.

articles.body:
Real Salt Lake have signed midfielder Taylor Booth on loan from Dutch Eredivisie side FC Twente, the club announced Wednesday.

The 25-year-old United States international's loan lasts through the 2027 MLS Sprint Season and includes a purchase option.

An RSL Academy product, Booth previously played for FC Utrecht in the Netherlands, SKN St. Pölten in Austria and Bayern Munich in Germany. Over his professional first-team career, Booth has produced 11g/8a in 94 games across all competitions.

Internationally, Booth has earned two USMNT caps and played in four matches at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

"Welcoming Taylor back to Utah was an easy decision for us," said RSL chief soccer officer Kurt Schmid.

"From his early days in our Academy to playing in top European leagues and representing the USMNT, he's established a remarkable track record. His tactical flexibility and dynamic attacking play bring immediate depth and quality as we push through the home stretch."

At RSL, Taylor joins his younger brother Zach Booth , who also returned to the club on loan in January.

The Claret-and-Cobalt sit 10th in the Western Conference with 28 points, one point outside of a Wild Card position.

articles.title: Everything Florida football coach Jon Sumrall said on his first SEC teleconference
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall discusses Florida's opener, QB room and more on SEC media call. Here's everything he had to say.
articles.body:
Florida football coach Jon Sumrall made his debut on the SEC's media teleconference call on Wednesday, Sept. 2.

This week's call will be one of five this season, which includes 10 minutes of questions for each of the conference's head coaches.

First-year coach Jon Sumrall will make his debut leading Florida against Florida Atlantic on Saturday, Sept. 5, with kickoff set for 7:45 p.m. at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. The game will be televised on the SEC Network.

Here's what Sumrall had to say on this week's media call.

"Yeah, our team, we had practice this morning. We play Saturday at 7:55 (sic) against FAU, and we're excited about it."

QUESTION: What are some non-negotiables for Florida in his first game as head coach?

Sumrall: "You got to play with enthusiasm and passion, effort, and you wanna see them strain. You only get 12 regular-season opportunities, and you don't want to take any of them for granted, ever. And I'd like for us to play like we've practiced, you know? Look like we've done some things before and operate efficiently. You see so many common mistakes that happen in Week 1 or Week 0 games like last week, and just for us to do what we've prepared in a crisp, clean manner is sort of the way you want to see it happen. But there will be guys making mistakes; when they do, I want to see them make them full speed. I want to see them go as hard as they can from the snap through the echo of the whistle."

QUESTION: How has the offensive line shown growth throughout the offseason, and where (offensive line coach) Phil Trautwein has shined ?

Sumrall: "Yeah, Phil is really detailed. He's a great teacher. He's very consistent. Phil's a guy who doesn't get too high or too low; he shows up the same way every day. Like I said, consistency is a key there, I think. And I think just finding ways to help guys maximize who they are. Different guys receive things in different ways from a coaching standpoint, and so, how we reach each player is a little bit unique. But he's very thorough with his preparation for his guys, and I think he's done a great job. I did not shy away from -- when we got here, I felt that the offensive line was an area that needed massive improvement. I think we've made improvement. Is it high enough for us to play the game at a level that we desire to? We're gonna find out real soon."

QUESTION: How will you feel when you run out of the tunnel ?

Sumrall: "I'm going to be pretty excited about it. I've said this a lot: I think back to when I was on the opposite sideline a couple times here as a player and as a coach, and how unique and special I've always felt like The Swamp is. And the fanbase here is so electric and charged up that I'll be very similarly wired. That gameday opportunity here is unlike many out there. And so, I'll be amped up. But at the end of the day too, it's really about focusing on us doing our job to the best of our ability and playing really good football. And so you have to make sure that while you're emotionally charged up and you're hyped, that you don't forget that the main things that go on within the game aren't in the stands; it's in between the white lines, and how do we help put our guys in situations to be successful."

QUESTION: What is the appreciation level of being an SEC head coach after growing up in the South ?

Sumrall: "I appreciate the shout out to Ronny Massey. What a great man. You know, I feel appreciation every day I walk into our building. We've got the Gator head logo above our main entrance, and every time I walk in our building, I get excited about being here. And I don't take any day at the office for granted. But, you know, to your point, growing up, I really idolized SEC football. I would watch every SEC game that was on TV or listen to a bunch of them on the radio as a kid, and to be able to have the privilege of leading an SEC team as a head coach is something I've dreamed about my entire coaching career. And, for me, it's the opportunity of a lifetime, and I will never take it for granted, and will always have great appreciation for the situation I'm in."

QUESTION: On how much more competitive the QB room has been from spring to fall?

Sumrall: "That's a great question. I'd say, if you asked me in early April who was going to start for us, it really wasn't much of a conversation, because of the difference in how well Philo operated at the line of scrimmage and ran the offense. The beautiful thing is Philo's continued to grow and get better, but so has the room. Tramell has stepped up and made strides. Aidan Warner has been really consistent and steady when he's had opportunities present. Will Griffin is uber talented, the freshman we got from Tampa. And then Aaron Williams is also in that room, does a great job adding value to our football team. But the whole room is elevated, which has made it more competitive, which is good for everybody. You know, you don't want anybody to become the starter because there's not great depth in the room. You want one guy just to elevate a little bit above the others, and I've got a lot of confidence in everybody in that quarterback room, though, that when they have opportunities, they're going to be ready to go."

QUESTION: A theme from you has been urgency for this team. You have to get to the game before you realize that, but is it where you want it to go into the season?

Sumrall: "I think it is, but you never know until you play. I think in preparation our urgency has improved. I think what you find out on Saturday is what your level of detail and doing your job at an elite level against another team, and it's not maybe in a practice environment against maybe people you play against every day. There's going to be some adversity hit in every game at every point all year. That's the biggest thing you can't really fully prepare for. We simulate a lot of things to try and create what that looks like around our building and practices all the time. But there's nothing like it happening in a live game. We'll see what our urgency looks like against another opponent here shortly. I look forward to seeing how we respond to a lot of different situations that come up within games."

QUESTION: From a special teams standpoint, not just kicking field goals, but overall how would you assess your special teams heading into Game 1?

Sumrall: "We've got Patrick Durkin as our starting field goal kicker. He was 25 of 28 last year and had a handful of them, I think four over 50 yards. So he's steady. He's got real ability. Yesterday on kickoffs, he was hitting most of them, eight, nine deep in the end zone, so he's got high touchback capability. Alec Clark is our punter who's been starting punter in college football now for a couple of years. He's really efficient, catch-to-kick. He's usually fast getting the ball off and really is a consistent punter in regard to distance and hang. I like how he does things. The other thing that Alec does at an elite level is he handles the short snaps really well on field goal and extra points. He's as good of a holder as I've ever been around, which probably doesn't get talked about enough. Snapping-wise, Carter Milliron will handle our long snaps on punt. He's played a lot of college football as a fifth-year senior. Then Lincoln Anderson is going to handle our short snaps, who is a true freshman from Hoover, Alabama, but has done a really good job this entire training camp and really shown that he is ready for this moment. Look forward to watching him perform, so those are our main specialists that will start and go on Saturday."

QUESTION: What were your first impressions of Jayden Woods? How far do you think he can go in his career?

Sumrall: "My first impression was positive, and it's only become more positive after that. He's a guy; when we got here, he was a high priority for us to retain. Then he made the decision to enter the transfer portal to just test the waters and see what was out there. We were able to hold on and get him to stay at the University of Florida, and I was pretty excited when that happened. I'm even more excited about the fact that he made the decision to stay each and every day that I get to work with him. He's really, really talented. But more so than just being talented, he's as good of a human you could ever want to be around. He works at a really high level. He's very detailed. He's got great pride in his craft, and he's a high-character guy. I think the sky is the limit for what Jayden can achieve on the field. But what makes it fun working with him day in, day out is just holistically he's a fantastic person. He has high standards for himself in every area of his life and not just football. He's going to be successful in any endeavor he takes on just because of the way he's wired. So very grateful he's on our football team. Like I said, I was excited off my first impression that we got to keep him. I'm even more excited now."

Reach Florida Gators writer Andrew Abadie at AAbadie@usatodayco.com or on X (formerly Twitter) at @AndrewAbadie . You can also find him on Facebook at Andrew Abadie Sports Reporter or on Instagram @andrewabadie_sports .

articles.title: Four Rays data points to watch into October
articles.summary: August and September are two of the most important months of the regular season for contenders. Rosters are galvanized in August following the trade deadline...
articles.body:
August and September are two of the most important months of the regular season for contenders. Rosters are galvanized in August following the trade deadline, and teams jockey for a higher postseason seed in September. There aren't too many "punt" games this time of the year now that magic numbers are counting down and managers can be aggressive with expanded rosters.

The Rays find themselves comfortable in control of their destiny and in the lead to win the AL East – securing a first-round bye. There are four key metrics I'll be following as they look to maintain their performance into October.

This Rays team is built on run prevention before anything else. Pitching and defense will determine how deep they play into October. So far this year, the Rays have been one of the top run prevention teams in the league. Only the Dodgers (69.1%) convert more batted balls into outs than the Rays (68.6%) this season. However, the Rays have been roughly average in this area since the beginning of August. Some of that is skewed by their west coast trip in which their flyball-to-out conversion rate dipped significantly playing in Denver and Sacramento and should rebound as they've been one of the best defensive outfields in the league this year. The infield has steadily improved throughout the year, and they've had the 9th best groundball-to-out rate since 8/1.

I'd like to see the team converting close to 69-70% of batted balls into outs by the end of the month. They're currently at 67.4% from August 1st through September 1st. This can be accomplished by playing better defense of course, but the pitching staff will need to continue to do their part and manage hard contact.

The back of the bullpen has been solid all year, and the addition of Tyler Wells at the deadline along with Manny Rodriguez return from injury only makes it better. The Rays bullpen has been the best in the league at holding leads since the beginning of August. Their 97.1% success rate for saves and holds is 3% better than the next closest team and about 10% better than league average. It may fluctuate a bit the rest of the season because baseball can be random, but the back of the bullpen is hitting their stride at the right time and will shorten games in October. I expect this to remain in the 90-95% range for the rest of the year and stay comfortably above average.

The overall performance of the bullpen has been negatively skewed by the performance of some middle relief options over the last month. Rather than just looking at just team reliever ERA, it can be beneficial to account for workload by factoring in total batters faced. ERA and FIP miss the workload aspect as they are calculated on a 9-inning basis.

Since 8/1, the Rays bullpen ranks 21st in the league in runs allowed per batter faced. Some of that is brought down by mop-up outings in blow outs, but that can't really happen as we head into October. Despite ranking in the bottom 10 in this metric, the Rays bullpen is only slightly below average. Additionally, there are plenty of internal candidates that could improve the bullpen.

They'll need at least one of Cleavinger, Booser, Sulser, Matz, or Legumina to step up and be the bridge to the back of the bullpen. I'm not concerned about this area; there's currently a surplus in the rotation with multiple players who will need their workloads managed as we approach the end of the season. A postseason pitching staff really only needs three true starters, so whoever isn't starting could transition to a relief role. Jax, McClanahan, and Seymour all make sense to move to multi or single inning relief roles to support the bullpen when fewer rotation spots are needed.

The Rays bullpen is currently at 0.126 runs per batter while the best bullpens are below 0.100. I'd like to see them closer to that number, so it'll be something to watch as the middle relief roles get sorted out over the next few weeks.

While the Rays might not have the roster to out-slug some of the other contenders, they can make up for it by maintaining an efficient offense. One way to measure efficiency is by looking at how many runs a team scores for each base they earn.

The Rays have the 4th best offensive efficiency since 8/1 in terms of runs per base at 0.277 and the league average is 0.255. They move runners well by bunting, stealing, and having productive outs more than most other teams. This has helped them maintain an above average offense for the season as a whole with a 105 wRC+. I'll be looking for them to maintain above-average offensive efficiency through October.

Overall, this team is in a good position with room to improve. I'd like to see the Rays get their outfield defense back to where it was earlier this season. The return of Mesa should help with that. I'd also like them to continue to hold leads and close games at the back of the bullpen while keeping games closer in middle relief. Rodriguez should help in that area, and I'm interested to see which of the current members of the rotation could transition to a relief role in October. I'll also be watching the group of Cleavinger, Booser, Sulser, Matz, and Legumina for those roles. And lastly, I want the Rays to stick to their identity and continue to manufacture runs with productive outs and taking an extra base as much as possible. We already know what we have in this team – they're legit World Series contenders, but performance in these four key areas is what will make or break their postseason run.

articles.title: Third-ranked Pegula, Medvedev power into US Open third round
articles.summary: World number three Jessica Pegula and former champion Daniil Medvedev raced into the third round of the US Open on Wednesday with straight-sets victories.He...
articles.body:
World number three Jessica Pegula and former champion Daniil Medvedev raced into the third round of the US Open on Wednesday with straight-sets victories.

Pegula needed just 56 minutes to trounce Sofia Kenin, the former Australian Open champion now ranked 110th, 6-3, 6-1.

Seventh-seeded Medvedev downed US wild card Sebastian Gorzny 6-1, 6-3, 7-5.

Pegula, who is among a trio of players who could supplant Aryna Sabalenka atop the world rankings in New York, dropped just seven points on serve.

"I was just trying to stay focused on what I needed to do," said the 2024 US Open runner-up, who next meets another former finalist, Leylah Fernandez.

The Canadian breezed past Thailand's Mananchaya Sawangkaew 6-4, 6-1.

Medvedev, who has struggled in the hard court build-up to the year's final Grand Slam, dominated 731st-ranked Gorzny.

He fired 14 aces and saved the lone break point he faced, although he was distracted briefly when a pair of small birds perched on the Louis Armstrong Stadium net and he was forced to replay a point he thought he'd won.

"I saw them straight away and I thought the point would stop straight away and we didn't," Medvedev said. "And the moment I hit the winner we stop. I was not happy with the decision."

He was happy enough with his game, however.

"The first two sets he was not playing the best tennis of his life maybe. The third set was much more competitive," Medvedev said.

"At the same time I feel like I had more break points and put more pressure on him."

Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka highlighted the day-four action.

World number one Sabalenka, gunning for a rare US Open three-peat, takes on 160th-ranked Russian qualifier Polina Iatcenko before second-ranked Alcaraz caps the night session against Portugal's Jaime Faria.

Alcaraz won his seventh major title at the Australian Open in January but arrived in New York an unknown quantity after a wrist injury forced a four-month layoff that saw him miss Roland Garros and Wimbledon.

He dispelled doubts with a straight-set victory over Roman Safiullin and will look for further improvement against 72nd-ranked Faria.

Other seeded players chasing third-round berths on Wednesday included eighth-seeded American Ben Shelton and his 11th-seeded compatriot Frances Tiafoe.

Brandon Nakashima, the in-form 16th seed who was also reckoned to be among the contenders to end American men's 23-year major title drought, was upset by 46th-ranked compatriot Alex Michelsen 6-3, 6-4, 6-4.

Meanwhile, sixth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur was hoping to finally get his campaign underway in a first-round match against Italian Andrea Guerrieri that was postponed from Tuesday by rain.

Spain's Paula Badosa, who was serving for her match when rain stopped play on Tuesday night, returned to finish off Australian Daria Kasatkina 6-1, 6-4 and book a second-round clash with fourth-seeded American Coco Gauff.

articles.title: ‘I’ve seen weirder things happen,’ Pirates not giving up on playoff hopes despite long odds
articles.summary: The Pirates are five games out of the third spot in the National League wild card race.
articles.body:
Tuesday's game between the Pirates and Giants at PNC Park on Tuesday night consisted of 25 runs, 34 hits, 12 walks, four hit batters and one crucial error.

All that resulted in a 13-12 win for the Pirates, who have now won three games in a row and five of their last seven after back-to-back series wins against the Padres and Cardinals.

"Eventful is a good way to put it," manager Don Kelly said after the game. "Getting a win any way you can get it."

With the win, the Pirates moved to 68-71 on the season and five games out of the third spot in the National League wild card race. The Phillies and Cubs are well above the rest of the pack. The Diamondbacks and Padres have been trading places between third and fourth in the standings. In between the two NL West foes and the Pirates are the Marlins and Cardinals.

A poor showing to start the second half served as a serious blow to Pittsburgh's playoff chances. According to Fangraphs, the Pirates have just a 2.5% chance of making the postseason, but the team isn't ready to throw in the towel.

"I've seen weirder things happen," Brandon Lowe said. "We've seen some incredible streaks happen. I've seen teams implode. I've been on teams that have imploded a little bit. Five games really isn't that much. People can say that it is. But it's not even a week's worth of games. Anything can happen. That's the biggest thing — we have to take care of things that we can take care of. We play our baseball, we'll see where we are in a few weeks."

articles.title: Big Ten topping SEC atop top 10 quarterback power rankings
articles.summary: The Big Ten has a quarterback in the top spot of CBS Sports' top 10 quarterback rankings.
articles.body:
CBS Sports unveiled its top 10 college football quarterback rankings on Wednesday, already sparking debate among fans.

Oregon quarterback Dante Moore headlines the list after a strong 2025 season, finishing with 3,565 yards through the air, 30 touchdowns, and 10 interceptions. He helped Oregon get to the College Football Playoff semifinals last year before losing to Indiana.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning is second on the list and had a nice end to the 2025 season, finishing with 3,163 yards through the air, 26 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. He hopes to lead Texas to the CFP this season after the program missed out last year.

Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, and Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin round out the top five. Chambliss and Sayin are returning to their respective schools, while Mensah will make his Miami debut this Friday against Stanford.

Mensah spent the 2025 season with Duke and helped the program win the ACC title over Virginia, finishing with 3,973 yards through the air, 34 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He transferred to Miami during the offseason and will try to help the program win the national title this season.

Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr, USC quarterback Jayden Maiava, Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover, SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings, and Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown round out the top 10.

Yes, Moore is ranked above Manning in these power rankings, which makes sense since Moore had the better 2025 campaign. However, both quarterbacks are among the top favorites for the Heisman Trophy this season.

We'll see how this list ages once we get further into the 2026 college football season.

articles.title: Steph Curry clears the air on his Warriors future after team's quiet offseason
articles.summary: Steph Curry addressed his future in Golden State by discussing the topic head-on.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors had a quiet offseason after missing out on a few high-profile names and potential trades, including LeBron James, who chose to head to the Philadelphia 76ers . The lack of moves fueled some speculation about star Steph Curry's future with the team, with many NBA fans calling for the Warriors to trade the future Hall of Famer.

However, through it all, Curry has given no indication that his tenure in Golden State would or could end anytime soon. It was actually just the opposite from Curry, who recently addressed his future with the Warriors in a recent interview with ABC7 News Bay Area .

I'm obviously excited for the season and trying to come in physically ready," Curry said. "[The] guys have been working all summer, I'm excited about the team we have coming back. The contract stuff, as it always goes, we'll solve it when it's time."

"The idea between now and training camp, our job is to collectively get ready for hopefully a retooled and re-energized and healthier year than we had last year, myself included. There's no secret I want to be here [for] the rest of my career, and making sure that it's the right situation and setup."

Obviously, this is good news for Warriors fans, and it's not all that surprising to hear from Curry himself. He's never strayed from the fact that he wants to be with the Warriors for his career in its entirety, and it doesn't appear that anything has changed as he heads into his 18th NBA season .

articles.title: Warriors' Steph Curry gets major contract extension update: 'There is no negotiation'
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors and Steph Curry knows a contract extension is available. However, the two have an interesting perspective on the situation with no...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors did not have the best offseason by any means, but they were able to bring back some familiar faces. The Warriors are entering the final stages of both Draymond Green and Steph Curry's careers.

However, Curry is expected to receive a contract extension at some point soon, and the deal is set to be a hefty one for this stage of his career.

"What the terms of a new extension look like for Curry will be completely up to him, as the Warriors are prepared to offer their star whatever he wants. If Steph wants the full $136.7 million through the 2028-29 season, he will get that. If he wants to take a discount to help the team, GM Mike Dunleavy Jr. will have no problem with said deal," NBA insider Brett Siegel wrote.

The only thing with Curry is that his extension has a lot riding on it.

"There's still players becoming contract extension eligible. By next week you'll start to see Steph Curry's name come up. On the 29th of August he's extension eligible for his contract. I have argued that it should be considered that Steph doesn't sign the extension yet. But if he doesn't sign his contract extension right now the Warriors could have over $100 million in salary cap space next summer," ESPN's Brian Windhorst said.

Windhorst also provided an update on Curry and whether the Warriors are currently negotiating with him. He explained that there is essentially no negotiation taking place, as the decision will ultimately come down to what Curry wants.

"It's not whether or not Steve is going to sign. It's what's on the plate. Just to give you guys some insight when you're over the age of 38 in the NBA you can only sign for a maximum of three years. This is an old rule from the '90s. And it's used to be over 36, but when Chris Paul and LeBron James were running the players association, they were getting close to their late 30's they pushed it to 38. Curry makes $62 million this year, so he can add 2 years onto it. Or he can do a 1 year max or just wait. The warriors are putting the decision in Steph's hands. There is no negotiation," Windhorst stated.

This is exactly how an organization should treat a franchise player. Curry has played a massive role in helping the Warriors win four NBA championships during his historic tenure with the franchise.

There is no doubt that Curry is going to get paid, but for now, both sides are remaining patient. As Windhorst mentioned, whatever Curry ultimately asks for is what Golden State is prepared to give him.

articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. (AP) — Patrick Mahomes appears on track to start for the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 against the Denver Broncos.

The two-time MVP has stated ever since he underwent surgery in December to repair torn ligaments in his left knee that his goal was to be on the field when the season begins.

And while doctors initially cautioned Mahomes that it could be October before he was ready to play, the quarterback surged past all expectations in his rehab, working with the first team throughout training camp.

Mahomes did not play in any preseason games. But that was always by design.

"He's going to keep practicing just like he's been doing," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, after their first practice following roster cuts. "These are more like practice here, a lot of one-versus-one play these next couple of days. That's a good thing."

The Chiefs will practice again Thursday before a long weekend, then resume work Monday. After that, they'll be into their game-week schedule, pointed toward a Monday night showdown between two of the favorites to win the AFC West this season.

One question looming over Mahomes' return: Will not playing in a preseason game affect his performance? The only other time he has gone an entire preseason without a game snap came during the pandemic, when all of the exhibition games were canceled.

"Me and Pat, we've kind of been working this offseason, the timing and stuff you need to work on," Chiefs wide receiver Xavier Worthy said, when asked about the rapport with his quarterback. "I feel like when it's time to play, we'll all be ready."

Worthy always thought Mahomes would be ready for the start of the season. In fact, he returned to Kansas City early this summer to work out with Mahomes, who was spending his days rehabbing his knee while watching World Cup games on TV.

"His will and want-to is beyond anything I've ever seen," Worthy said. "He kind of leads the team in that way. You have your leader leading like that and guys fall behind. He's just a 'will' guy, always willing to work."

Exactly who is protecting Mahomes should he play Week 1 is another question mark.

Left tackle Josh Simmons remained out of practice Wednesday with a lingering back injury, forcing Kansas City to shuffle the offensive line. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has been moving around in his absence, while Jaylon Moore has also gotten first-team reps.

Perhaps wary of the injury woes up front — guard Trey Smith has been dealing with a hip injury — the Chiefs made a couple of moves to build their depth in recent days. They sent a conditional sixth-round pick to Baltimore for undrafted rookie Diego Pounds, and they acquired Joshua Ezeudu from the Giants for a seventh-round selection.

"It's just a matter of them getting adjusted to everything, from the snap count to the plays to the calls to the pass protection," Reid said. "It was great to get them in there. There were a couple of hiccups in there but for the most part they did a great job."

articles.body:
Normally, after completed transfers, we are used to seeing different images: stars proudly wearing the shirt of their new club or smiling for the camera as they sign their contract.

Very late on Deadline Day, different scenes reached us from Spain: on Monday night, after his departure from Real Betis was confirmed, Pablo García left the club grounds alongside his mother — both were in tears.

That was shown in videos on 'X' — recorded by journalists and fans who had come to the grounds to say goodbye to him.

The 20-year-old youngster's move to newly promoted La Liga side Racing Santander is the very symbol of a shattered dream.

According to reports, García had no intention whatsoever of leaving the club where he had learned to play football from a very young age. He had been part of the club for 15 years.

According to Spanish media reports, Betis sold him to make room in the squad structure — specifically for returning player Dani Ceballos.

Fans online are heavily criticizing the club's management for this decision.

García himself was quoted after the tearful farewell at the club grounds, before his departure at the airport, as saying: "It is a very difficult time for everyone, but we have to keep our heads up and look forward." This comes from a report by 'Kicker'.

He said he hopes to return, and that there had been many things he had not been able to influence: "I wish everything had turned out the way we had hoped."

What makes it especially bitter is that García actually had every reason to hope he would make his breakthrough at his youth club this year. He came on as a substitute in all three league matches and even scored the winner against Valencia.

What do you think? Does the emotional farewell and disappointment affect you, or is this simply the other side of the coin in the sometimes ruthless football business?
